records.name: Running a push rule in transparent mode
records.purpose: Extends a completed move to a further Location without adding an operation, by rewriting its destination and its date, and walks a chain of such rules.

operands.name: move date
operands.constraints: the completion instant

operands.name: lead time of the rule
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: destination Location of the rule
operands.constraints: written onto the move

operands.name: detail lines of the move
operands.constraints: their destination Locations are re-pointed

preconditions.condition: The selected rule's action is the automatic mode that adds no operation.
preconditions.otherwise: The manual mode applies and a new move is created instead.

procedure: Remember the move's current destination Location.
Compute the new date as the move's date plus the rule's lead time in days, and write it together with the rule's destination Location onto the move.
Re-point the detail lines: their destination Location becomes the put-away result for the new destination Location, or that Location itself when put-away returns nothing.
When the destination Location actually changed, run the push step again on the same move and return the first new move it produces, which walks a chain of transparent rules.
Stop the recursion when the destination Location did not change.
records.formula: new date = move date + rule lead time in days ; new destination Location = the rule's destination Location ; each line's destination Location = the put-away result for the new destination Location , or that Location itself

rounding.what: Nothing in the date arithmetic; the put-away that follows applies its own rounding.
rounding.precision: Whole days for the lead time.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step of the date arithmetic.

result.name: the rewritten move and the first move a chained rule produced
result.unit_or_currency: an instant, a Location and possibly a new move
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the move and on its detail lines.

edge_cases.case: The destination Location did not change.
edge_cases.outcome: The recursion stops, which is what terminates a chain of transparent rules.

edge_cases.case: Put-away returns nothing for the new destination Location.
edge_cases.outcome: The lines are pointed at that Location itself.

edge_cases.case: A further transparent rule applies at the new destination.
edge_cases.outcome: The push step runs again on the same move and the chain is walked.

edge_cases.case: The rule's lead time is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The move's date is unchanged.

worked_examples.description: A transparent rule with a lead time of two days
worked_examples.narrative: The move now ends two days later in the stock Location, its lines are put away into the first bin, and the push step runs again because the destination Location changed.

records.name: Running a push rule that adds an operation
records.purpose: Creates the continuation move when a push rule adds an operation, deciding its demand, its Locations, its company and its supply method.

operands.name: processed quantity and demand of the original move
operands.unit_or_currency: the line unit of the move
operands.constraints: the demand is used only when it is negative

operands.name: origin of the original move
operands.source: the move, else the Transfer reference, else the single character `/`
operands.constraints: reproduced as it stands

operands.name: destination Location of the rule
operands.constraints: overridden in the two cases below

operands.name: final Location of the original move
operands.constraints: overrides the rule's destination when it is a descendant of it

operands.name: contact of the original move
operands.constraints: its own customer Location overrides the destination when the rule's destination has customer usage

operands.name: lead time of the rule
operands.constraints: added to the move's date

preconditions.condition: The selected rule's action is the mode that adds an operation.
preconditions.otherwise: The transparent mode applies and the move itself is rewritten.

procedure: Compute the new date as the move's date plus the rule's lead time in days.
Set the new move's demand to the original move's processed quantity, or to its demand when that demand is negative.
Set the origin to the move's origin, else the Transfer reference, else the single character `/`.
Set the source Location to the original move's destination Location.

Set the destination Location to the rule's destination Location, overridden by the move's final Location when that final Location is a descendant of the rule's destination Location, and overridden by the contact's own customer Location when the move has a contact and the rule's destination Location has customer usage.
Set the final Location to the move's final Location when the move's destination Location is not already inside it, and to nothing otherwise.

Set the rule, the new date, the move's deadline, the company as the rule's company else the rule's Warehouse's else the Operation Type's Warehouse's, no Transfer, the rule's Operation Type, the rule's propagate-cancel flag, the Warehouse as the rule's else the move's destination Location's, and the advanced supply method.
Copy the move with those values.
When the new move must skip the push step, force its destination Location to its final Location.
When the new move bypasses reservation, force its supply method to take from stock.
When the new move's source Location does not bypass reservation, link the new move as a destination move of the original.
Return the new move.
records.formula: new demand = the original move's processed quantity , or its demand when that demand is negative ; new date = move date + rule lead time in days ; new source Location = the original move's destination Location ; new destination Location = the rule's destination Location , overridden by the move's final Location when that is a descendant of it , and by the contact's customer Location when the rule's destination has customer usage

rounding.what: Nothing; the demand is copied and the date arithmetic is in whole days.
rounding.precision: Whole days for the lead time.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the new Stock Move
result.unit_or_currency: a demand in the line unit and a set of Locations and dates
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored; it is confirmed with elevated rights together with the other new moves.

edge_cases.case: The original move's demand is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The new move takes that negative demand instead of the processed quantity.

edge_cases.case: The move has no origin and no Transfer reference.
edge_cases.outcome: The origin becomes the single character `/`.

edge_cases.case: The move's final Location is a descendant of the rule's destination.
edge_cases.outcome: The final Location overrides the rule's destination, so the goods go straight to where they are really needed.

edge_cases.case: The rule's destination Location has customer usage and the move has a contact.
edge_cases.outcome: The contact's own customer Location overrides the destination.

edge_cases.case: The new move bypasses reservation.
edge_cases.outcome: Its supply method is forced to take from stock rather than left as advanced.

records.name: Re-wiring the chain after a push rule has run
records.purpose: Repairs the links of the moves that used to follow the pushed move, propagating them onto the new move where that makes sense and breaking them where it does not.

operands.name: destination moves of the original move
operands.constraints: the newly created move is excluded from the walk

operands.name: final Location of the original move
operands.constraints: required for a destination move to be propagated

operands.name: source Location of each destination move
operands.constraints: compared against the final Location and against the original's destination Location

operands.name: the newly created move
operands.source: the push rule that just ran
operands.constraints: the target of a propagated link

preconditions.condition: A push rule has just run on the original move.
preconditions.otherwise: The chain is left alone.

procedure: For each destination move of the original that is not the newly created one, decide between propagation and breaking.

Propagate the destination move when a new move was created, the original has a final Location and the destination move's source Location equals that final Location: unlink it from the original and link it to the new move instead.

Otherwise, when the destination move's source Location is not inside the original's destination Location, break the link: the destination move loses the originating link, its supply method is reset to take from stock and its status is recomputed.
Leave the link untouched in every other case.
Confirm all the new moves with elevated rights.
records.formula: a destination move is propagated when a new move exists , the original has a final Location and the destination move's source Location = that final Location ; a link is broken when the destination move's source Location is not inside the original's destination Location

rounding.what: Nothing; the decision compares Locations.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the re-wired chain links and the recomputed statuses
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the moves.

edge_cases.case: No new move was created, the rule being transparent.
edge_cases.outcome: No link is propagated; a link is only broken when its source Location is outside the original's destination Location.

edge_cases.case: The destination move's source Location is inside the original's destination Location.
edge_cases.outcome: The link is left untouched, because the goods will still be there for it.

edge_cases.case: The original has no final Location.
edge_cases.outcome: No propagation is possible and only the breaking test applies.

edge_cases.case: A link is broken.
edge_cases.outcome: The destination move falls back to taking from stock and its status is recomputed, so it competes for goods like any unchained move.

records.name: Creating the Transfer backorder
records.purpose: Moves the unfinished moves of a validated Transfer into a new Transfer linked to it, so that the remaining demand keeps its own document.

operands.name: moves of the Transfer whose status is neither done nor cancelled
operands.constraints: or the explicit list supplied by the split action, restricted to the Transfer

operands.name: status of each carried-over move
operands.source: the move, recomputed before the decision
operands.constraints: must be recomputed first

operands.name: reference of the original Transfer
operands.constraints: the backorder is created with an empty reference and draws its own

operands.unit_or_currency: a choice of manual, at confirmation or before the scheduled date
operands.source: the Operation Type of the backorder
operands.constraints: decides whether the availability is checked at once

preconditions.condition: At least one move of the Transfer is neither done nor cancelled.
preconditions.otherwise: No backorder is created.

preconditions.condition: Backorders are not forbidden for this validation.
preconditions.otherwise: The step is not reached at all.

procedure: Determine the moves to carry over: those of the Transfer whose status is neither done nor cancelled, or, when an explicit list is supplied by the split action, that list restricted to the Transfer.
Recompute the statuses of those moves.
When there are none, create no backorder.
Copy the Transfer with an empty reference, no moves, no detail lines, the original as the back-order link and the same return link.
Move the carried-over moves and their detail lines into the backorder and clear their picked flag.
Clear the backorder's responsible.
Post on the original Transfer the note that the backorder, named by a link to it, has been created.
When the backorder's Operation Type reserves at confirmation, run the availability check on it.
records.formula: the backorder carries exactly the moves whose status is neither done nor cancelled ; it is created with an empty reference , the original as its back-order link , the same return link , no responsible , and its moves' picked flags cleared

rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit, inside the availability check.
rounding.method: Comparison at the step, inside the availability check.

records.name: The validation algorithm of a set of Transfers
records.purpose: The complete sequence performed when a person validates one or more Transfers, from the immediate-transfer step through the sanity check and the backorder question to the completion and the follow-up actions.

operands.name: working set of Transfers
operands.constraints: the ones already done are dropped

operands.name: moves and detail lines of each Transfer
operands.constraints: decide the sanity check and the backorder question

operands.name: backorder policy of each Operation Type
operands.constraints: splits the working set at the completion step

operands.name: Transfers declared as not to be backordered
operands.source: the calling context, set by the backorder screen
operands.constraints: optional

operands.name: suppression flags
operands.constraints: the sanity check, the backorder question and the text-message warning can each be suppressed

preconditions.condition: The immediate-transfer step precedes the sanity check.
preconditions.otherwise: A Transfer created and validated in one gesture would be refused for having no quantity.

preconditions.condition: The picked marking precedes the backorder decision.
preconditions.otherwise: Every line would look unpicked and a backorder would always be proposed.

procedure: Drop the Transfers that are already done from the working set.

Confirm the Transfers of the working set that are in draft; then, for every move of those draft Transfers whose processed quantity is zero while its demand is not, copy the demand into the processed quantity.

Unless the caller suppressed it, run the sanity check: decide per Transfer whether it has no quantity at all, collect the Transfers with no moves and no detail lines, collect the lines that need a lot, and report the failures in the single-Transfer form or in the several-Transfer form.
Remember the identifiers of the Transfers being validated in the calling context, so that a wizard can resume the validation.
For each Transfer, when at least one move has a processed quantity and no move other than the scrap moves is picked, mark every move of the Transfer as picked.
Unless the backorder step is suppressed, run the backorder decision; when it returns a set of Transfers, open the backorder screen on them and stop, the validation resuming when the person answers.

Run the text-message warning: when the company has text-message validation on, the Operation Type is a delivery, the contact has a telephone number and the company has not yet been warned, open the one-time warning screen and stop.

Split the working set: the Transfers not to be backordered are those whose Operation Type never creates backorders, plus, when the calling context names Transfers that must not be backordered, those of them whose Operation Type does not always create backorders; the rest are to be backordered.
Complete the first group with backorders forbidden, then the second group with backorders allowed.

Complete a Transfer by running the company consistency check, writing the Transfer's owner onto every move as owner restriction and onto every detail line as owner, running the move completion on the moves whose status is draft, waiting another move, partially available, assigned or waiting, stamping the completion instant, resetting the priority to normal, re-reserving downstream, unpacking inter-company containers and sending the confirmation message and the confirmation text message.
Collect the print actions the Operation Types ask for.

When the user is in the reception-report group and at least one validated Transfer's Operation Type asks to show the report, collect the moves of those Transfers that are storable, not cancelled, have a processed quantity and have no destination move; when there are any and at least one open move in the same Warehouse, excluding vendor Locations and excluding the validated Transfers themselves, demands one of those products, open the report.
Return the report action directly when there is no print action, and otherwise as the follow-up action of the print action.
Return the print action when there is one, and otherwise a plain success.
records.formula: the working set is split into the Transfers completed with backorders forbidden and those completed with backorders allowed ; a Transfer is completed only after the sanity check , the picked marking and the backorder decision have run in that order

rounding.what: The zero-quantity test of the sanity check and the comparison of the picked quantity against the demand in the backorder decision.
rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` decimal precision, a digit count, for both.
rounding.step: Once per move, inside the sanity check and inside the backorder decision.

result.name: the completed Transfers, their backorders and the follow-up actions
result.unit_or_currency: quantities in each move's line unit and instants
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Transfers, the moves, the lines and the Stock Quantity records; the print and report actions are returned to the screen.

edge_cases.case: A Transfer is created and validated in one gesture.
edge_cases.outcome: The immediate-transfer step copies the demand into the processed quantity before the sanity check, so the Transfer is not refused for having no quantity.

edge_cases.case: A whole batch is validated.
edge_cases.outcome: The per-Transfer sanity check is suppressed, because the batch has already run it once over the whole set.

edge_cases.case: The person answers the backorder question.
edge_cases.outcome: The validation resumes with the backorder step suppressed and with the Transfers the person declared as not to be backordered named in the calling context.

edge_cases.case: Several Transfers fail the sanity check.
edge_cases.outcome: One message is built, with the empty ones and the ones missing lots each contributing their own sentence, and the zero-quantity case is not reported in that form.

edge_cases.case: The Operation Type never creates backorders.
edge_cases.outcome: The Transfer is completed with backorders forbidden, so its short moves are cancelled instead of being carried over.

operands.constraints: a digit count, used for the comparison

preconditions.condition: The Operation Type's backorder policy is to ask.
preconditions.otherwise: The Transfer is skipped, because a policy of always or never needs no decision.

procedure: Skip every Transfer whose Operation Type does not ask, meaning whose backorder policy is always or never.
For each move of a remaining Transfer that is not cancelled, test the first trigger: the move has a non-zero demand and is not picked.
Test the second trigger: the move's picked quantity is strictly less than its demand at the Product Unit precision.

Compute the picked quantity of a move as the sum, over its picked lines only, of their quantities converted into the move's line unit without rounding, when the move is picked but at least one of its lines is not.
Compute it as the move's whole processed quantity in every other case.
Return the Transfers for which at least one move satisfies either trigger.
records.formula: picked quantity(move) = sum over the picked lines of convert( line quantity , line unit , move line unit , none ) , when the move is picked and at least one of its lines is not ; = the move's processed quantity , otherwise ; a Transfer needs a decision when any of its non-cancelled moves has a non-zero demand and is not picked , or has picked quantity < demand at the Product Unit precision

rounding.what: The comparison of the picked quantity against the demand; the conversions inside the picked quantity are deliberately unrounded.
rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` decimal precision, a digit count, for the comparison; none for the conversions.
rounding.step: Once per move, after the picked quantity is known.

result.name: the Transfers that need a backorder decision
result.stored_or_displayed: Passed to the backorder screen; never stored.

edge_cases.case: A move is over-processed.
edge_cases.outcome: Its picked quantity exceeds its demand, so neither trigger fires and no question is asked for it.

edge_cases.case: A move is picked while some of its lines are not.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the picked lines count towards the picked quantity, so the unticked part triggers the question.

edge_cases.case: A move has a zero demand and is not picked.
edge_cases.outcome: The first trigger does not fire, because it requires a non-zero demand.

edge_cases.case: The policy is always or never.
edge_cases.outcome: The Transfer is skipped and the completion decides on its own.

worked_examples.description: The fourth step of the second worked trace of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The Bolt move is picked and its picked quantity is not below its demand, so neither trigger fires; the Paint move has a non-zero demand and is not picked, which fires the first trigger and opens the backorder screen.

worked_examples.description: A move picked with only one of its two lines ticked
worked_examples.narrative: The move is picked but one line is not, so only the ticked four count; four is strictly below the demand of twelve at the digit count and the question is asked.

records.name: Re-reservation after a completion
records.purpose: Looks for the open moves that the goods just received could satisfy and reserves them, letting the document that caused the arrival claim it before anyone else.

operands.name: completed moves of a receipt or an internal transfer
operands.source: the validation that has just completed
operands.constraints: only those Operation Type kinds trigger the search

operands.name: destination Locations of the completed moves
operands.constraints: each one, together with its ancestors, forms part of the filter

operands.name: products of the completed moves
operands.constraints: restrict the candidate moves

operands.name: reservation date of each candidate move
operands.constraints: must be on or before today unless the Operation Type reserves at confirmation

operands.name: document references of the completing moves
operands.constraints: used to re-sort the candidates

preconditions.condition: The system parameter that disables automatic reservation is not set.
preconditions.otherwise: The search is skipped entirely.

preconditions.condition: The Operation Type of the completed Transfer is a receipt or an internal transfer.
preconditions.otherwise: The search does not run, which is why a delivery does not trigger it.

procedure: Skip entirely when the system parameter that disables automatic reservation is set.

Build the product-and-location filter: for each distinct destination Location among the completed moves, take the moves of those products whose source Location is that Location or one of its ancestors.

Add the static conditions: the status is confirmed or partially available; the supply method is take from stock; and either the reservation date is on or before today or the Operation Type reserves at confirmation.
Order the result by priority descending, then by date ascending, then by identifier ascending.
Re-sort it so that the moves sharing a document reference with the completing moves come first.
Run the reservation on the result.
records.formula: candidates = { open moves of the completed products whose source Location is a completed destination Location or one of its ancestors , whose status is confirmed or partially available , whose supply method is take from stock , and whose reservation date ≤ today or whose Operation Type reserves at confirmation } , ordered by priority descending , date ascending , identifier ascending , then by sharing a document reference with the completing moves

rounding.what: Nothing in the search; the reservation that follows applies its own rounding.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit, inside the reservation.
rounding.method: Comparison at the step, inside the reservation.
rounding.step: Only inside the reservation.

result.name: the re-reserved moves
result.unit_or_currency: quantities in each move's line unit
result.stored_or_displayed: The reservation stores detail lines and raises reserved counters.

edge_cases.case: The completed Transfer is a delivery.
edge_cases.outcome: The search does not run at all.

edge_cases.case: A candidate shares a document reference with a completing move.
edge_cases.outcome: It is placed first, so the document that caused the arrival claims it.

edge_cases.case: A candidate's supply method is advanced.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, because it must wait for its own supplying move.

edge_cases.case: A candidate's source Location is an ancestor of the destination Location.
edge_cases.outcome: It is included, so a move reserving at the warehouse level picks up goods put into one of its shelves.

worked_examples.description: A receipt of ten units into the stock Location while two deliveries wait for the product
worked_examples.narrative: The plain ordering puts the earlier move first, but the move sharing a document reference with the receipt is moved in front, so the document that caused the arrival is served first.

worked_examples.description: The seventh step of the second worked trace of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The Operation Type is a delivery, so the re-reservation search does not run after that validation.

records.name: Inter-company unpacking at validation
records.purpose: Empties the containers of a transit movement between two companies, so that the receiving company handles loose goods rather than the sending company's containers.

operands.name: contact of the validated Transfer
operands.constraints: the company is looked up from it or from one of its ancestors

operands.name: company whose contact is that contact or one of its ancestors
operands.constraints: must differ from the Transfer's company

operands.name: company of the Transfer
operands.constraints: compared against the company found

operands.name: destination containers of the moves whose destination Location has transit usage
operands.constraints: these are the containers unpacked

preconditions.condition: The container group is active and the system parameter that unpacks inter-company containers is set.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is unpacked.

preconditions.condition: The Transfer has a contact.
preconditions.otherwise: No company can be looked up and nothing is unpacked.

procedure: When the container group is active and the system parameter that unpacks inter-company containers is set, take each validated Transfer that has a contact.
Find the company whose contact is that contact or one of its ancestors.
When that company differs from the Transfer's company, unpack the destination containers of every move whose destination Location has transit usage.
Do nothing when no such company is found, or when it is the Transfer's own company.
records.formula: the destination containers of the transit moves are unpacked when the container group is active , the system parameter is set , the Transfer has a contact , and the company whose contact is that contact or one of its ancestors ≠ the Transfer's company

rounding.what: Nothing; the unpacking that follows applies its own housekeeping.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the unpacked containers and their relocated goods
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the containers and on the Stock Quantity records.

edge_cases.case: The contact belongs to the Transfer's own company.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is unpacked, because the movement is not between two companies.

edge_cases.case: The move's destination Location has no transit usage.
edge_cases.outcome: Its containers are left alone.

edge_cases.case: The container group is not active.
edge_cases.outcome: The step does not run.

edge_cases.case: The system parameter is not set.
edge_cases.outcome: The step does not run even for a genuine inter-company transit.

worked_examples.description: A resupply from one company to another through a transit Location
worked_examples.narrative: The contact belongs to another company, so the container of the transit move is unpacked and the receiving company takes the goods loose.

records.name: Over-processing a move
records.purpose: States what happens when more is recorded than was demanded: the surplus simply travels, no extra record is created and no backorder arises.

operands.name: demand of the move
operands.unit_or_currency: the line unit of the move
operands.constraints: unchanged by the over-processing

operands.name: processed quantity of the move
operands.unit_or_currency: the line unit of the move
operands.source: the move, recomputed from its detail lines
operands.constraints: strictly greater than the demand

operands.name: source Location usage
operands.source: the source Location of the move
operands.constraints: decides where the surplus comes from

preconditions.condition: The processed quantity strictly exceeds the demand.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary backorder tests apply.

procedure: Let the move's processed quantity simply exceed its demand; the demand is not raised.
Skip the backorder move, because the backorder test compares the processed quantity against the demand and finds the processed quantity greater.
Skip the backorder question, because the backorder decision finds the picked quantity greater than the demand.
Let the status recomputation mark the move assigned before the completion, because it finds the processed quantity greater than or equal to the demand.
Let the extra quantity reach the destination through the detail lines exactly like the rest.

Take the surplus from the source: for a Location that bypasses reservation the goods are simply created; for an internal Location the extra quantity drives the available quantity negative, which frees other reservations and may leave a negative quantity record behind.
records.formula: no backorder move arises , because the test requires processed quantity < demand ; no backorder question is asked , because the test requires picked quantity < demand ; the move's status is assigned , because processed quantity ≥ demand ; the destination receives the whole processed quantity

rounding.what: The two comparisons of the processed quantity against the demand.
rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` decimal precision, a digit count, for both the backorder test and the backorder question; the line unit's rounding step for the status recomputation.
rounding.method: Comparison at the digit count and at the step.
rounding.step: Once per move, at each of the three tests.

result.name: the completed move with a processed quantity above its demand
result.unit_or_currency: the line unit of the move
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored; the surplus quantity reaches the destination Location.

edge_cases.case: The source Location bypasses reservation.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus goods are simply created, which is the ordinary case of receiving more than was ordered.

edge_cases.case: The source Location is internal.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus drives the available quantity negative, which frees other reservations and may leave a negative record behind.

edge_cases.case: The move is part of a Transfer whose other moves are short.
edge_cases.outcome: Those other moves are still carried into a backorder; the over-processed move contributes nothing to it.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: A receipt demands ten and twelve are received; the demand stays at ten, the processed quantity is twelve, the move completes, no backorder is created and twelve units arrive in stock.

records.name: Deadline propagation along a chain of moves
records.purpose: Shifts the deadline of every move of a chain by the same amount when one of them changes, so that a delay at one step is visible at every other.

operands.name: old deadline of the move
operands.constraints: the difference is zero when the move had no deadline

operands.name: new deadline of the move
operands.constraints: written on the move and propagated

operands.name: linked moves upstream and downstream
operands.source: the originating and destination links of the move
operands.constraints: only those that are neither done nor cancelled and that have not already been visited

operands.name: set of already visited moves
operands.constraints: remembered so that the propagation cannot loop

preconditions.condition: The set of moves being written is remembered in the calling context.
preconditions.otherwise: The propagation would revisit a move it has already shifted and could loop.

procedure: Remember the set of moves being written in the calling context so that the propagation cannot loop.
For each move, let the difference be the old deadline less the new deadline, or zero when the move had no deadline.

For every move linked to it upstream or downstream that is neither done nor cancelled and that has not already been visited: when it has a deadline and the difference is non-zero, subtract the difference from its deadline, shifting the whole chain by the same amount.
Otherwise, when it has no deadline or a different one, set its deadline to the new deadline.
records.formula: difference = old deadline − new deadline , or zero when the move had no deadline ; for a linked move with a deadline and a non-zero difference: its deadline = its deadline − difference ; for a linked move with no deadline or a different one: its deadline = the new deadline

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the deadlines of the chain's moves
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the moves and rolled up into the deadline of each Transfer.

edge_cases.case: The move had no deadline before the write.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero, so every linked move simply takes the new deadline.

edge_cases.case: A linked move is done or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not touched.

edge_cases.case: A linked move has already been visited.
edge_cases.outcome: It is skipped, which is what stops the propagation from looping.

edge_cases.case: A linked move already carries exactly the new deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is written for it, because the second branch requires no deadline or a different one.

worked_examples.description: Pushing a deadline back by two days on a chain of two moves
worked_examples.narrative: The difference is minus two days, so subtracting it from the linked move's deadline moves it two days later as well, and the whole chain keeps its internal spacing.

worked_examples.description: Setting a deadline on a move that had none
worked_examples.narrative: With no old deadline the difference is zero, so every linked move simply takes the new deadline.

related_rules: business-rules.md switch that remembers the visited moves of a deadline propagation

records.name: The delay alert date of a move and of a Transfer
records.purpose: Shows when a move is being held up by a predecessor that is scheduled later than the move itself, and posts a note on the affected documents when a deadline moves because of it.

operands.name: dates of the originating moves
operands.source: the moves that supply this one, restricted to those that are neither done nor cancelled
operands.constraints: the maximum is taken

operands.name: date of the move itself
operands.constraints: the maximum must be strictly later for the alert to exist

operands.name: dates of the moves of a Transfer
operands.constraints: the Transfer's alert is the maximum over its moves

operands.name: name of the upstream document
operands.source: the document causing the delay, used in the note
operands.constraints: placed in the note's subject and body

preconditions.condition: The move has at least one originating move that is neither done nor cancelled.
preconditions.otherwise: The alert date is empty.

procedure: Take the dates of the originating moves that are neither done nor cancelled and compute their maximum.
When that maximum is strictly later than the move's own date, the alert date is that maximum.
Otherwise the alert date is empty.
Take the maximum over its moves as a Transfer's delay alert date.

When the deadline of a move changes because of an upstream delay, post a note on the affected documents with the subject naming the upstream document and the body saying that the deadline has been automatically updated because of a delay on that document, given as a link.
Skip the note when the document's most recent message already carries that subject.
records.formula: delay alert date(move) = maximum( the dates of the originating moves that are neither done nor cancelled ) , when that maximum is strictly later than the move's own date ; = empty , otherwise ; delay alert date(transfer) = the maximum over its moves

rounding.what: Nothing; the comparison is on instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: delay alert date
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the move and on the Transfer as the alert that a predecessor is late.

edge_cases.case: Every originating move is done or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: No date competes and the alert is empty.

edge_cases.case: The maximum equals the move's own date.
edge_cases.outcome: The alert is empty, because the comparison is strictly later.

edge_cases.case: The document's most recent message already carries the alert subject.
edge_cases.outcome: No new note is posted, so a repeated shift does not flood the document.

worked_examples.description: A delivery whose supplying receipt is scheduled after it
worked_examples.narrative: The predecessor is scheduled two days after the move itself, so the alert shows the sixteenth of September.

worked_examples.description: The same delivery once the receipt has been brought forward
worked_examples.narrative: The maximum is earlier than the move's own date, so no alert is shown.

records.name: The scheduled date of a Transfer shipping as soon as possible
records.purpose: Gives the date a Transfer is planned for when its goods may leave as soon as each is ready, which is the earliest of its open moves.

operands.name: dates of the moves that are neither done nor cancelled
operands.constraints: the minimum is taken

operands.name: previous value of the scheduled date
operands.constraints: the fallback when no move qualifies

operands.name: current instant
operands.constraints: the last fallback

preconditions.condition: The Transfer's shipping policy is to ship as soon as possible.
preconditions.otherwise: The all-at-once variant applies and the maximum is taken instead.

procedure: Take the dates of the Transfer's moves that are neither done nor cancelled.
Take their minimum.
Fall back to the previous value of the scheduled date, and then to the current instant, when no move qualifies.
records.formula: scheduled date = minimum( the dates of the moves that are neither done nor cancelled ) , with the previous value, or the current instant, as the fallback when there are no such moves

rounding.what: Nothing; the minimum is taken over instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: scheduled date of the Transfer
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Transfer, shown in the operation overview graph and compared against the deadline.

edge_cases.case: Every move is done or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The previous value is kept, or the current instant is taken when there was none.

edge_cases.case: The Transfer is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: Writing the scheduled date is refused with the message that the scheduled date of a cancelled transfer may not be changed.

edge_cases.case: One move is much later than the others.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not move the scheduled date, because the earliest wins under this policy.

worked_examples.description: A delivery of two open moves scheduled three days apart
worked_examples.narrative: The earliest of the two open moves is taken, so the Transfer is planned for the twelfth of September.

records.name: The scheduled date of a Transfer shipping all at once
records.purpose: Gives the date a Transfer is planned for when every one of its goods must leave together, which is the latest of its open moves.

operands.name: dates of the moves that are neither done nor cancelled
operands.constraints: the maximum is taken

operands.name: previous value of the scheduled date
operands.constraints: the fallback when no move qualifies

operands.name: current instant
operands.constraints: the last fallback

preconditions.condition: The Transfer's shipping policy is to ship all at once.
preconditions.otherwise: The as-soon-as-possible variant applies and the minimum is taken instead.

procedure: Take the dates of the Transfer's moves that are neither done nor cancelled.
Take their maximum.
Fall back to the previous value of the scheduled date, and then to the current instant, when no move qualifies.
records.formula: scheduled date = maximum( the dates of the moves that are neither done nor cancelled ) , with the previous value, or the current instant, as the fallback when there are no such moves

rounding.what: Nothing; the maximum is taken over instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: scheduled date of the Transfer
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Transfer, shown in the operation overview graph and compared against the deadline.

edge_cases.case: Every move is done or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The previous value is kept, or the current instant is taken when there was none.

edge_cases.case: One move is much later than the others.
edge_cases.outcome: It sets the scheduled date, because the whole Transfer must wait for it.

edge_cases.case: The Transfer's moves are merged.
edge_cases.outcome: The merged move takes the maximum of the group's dates as well, by the same principle.

worked_examples.description: The same two open moves under the all-at-once policy
worked_examples.narrative: The latest of the two open moves is taken, so the Transfer is planned for the fifteenth of September, when both parts can leave together.

records.name: The deadline of a Transfer shipping as soon as possible
records.purpose: Gives the date by which a Transfer is committed when its goods may leave as soon as each is ready, which is the earliest deadline among its moves.

operands.name: deadlines of the non-cancelled moves that have one
operands.constraints: moves without a deadline do not compete

operands.name: shipping policy
operands.unit_or_currency: as soon as possible, or all at once
operands.constraints: must be as soon as possible for this variant

preconditions.condition: At least one non-cancelled move carries a deadline.
preconditions.otherwise: The Transfer's deadline is empty.

procedure: Take the deadlines of the Transfer's non-cancelled moves that have one.
Take their minimum.
Leave the Transfer's deadline empty when no move carries one.
records.formula: deadline = minimum( the deadlines of the non-cancelled moves that have one ) , when the shipping policy is as soon as possible

rounding.what: Nothing; the minimum is taken over instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: deadline of the Transfer
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Transfer and compared against its scheduled date to raise the deadline issue indicator.

edge_cases.case: No move carries a deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The Transfer's deadline is empty and no deadline issue can arise.

edge_cases.case: A cancelled move carries a deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not compete, because only the non-cancelled moves are taken.

edge_cases.case: A done move carries a deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: It does compete, because only cancellation excludes a move here.

worked_examples.description: A delivery whose two moves are committed three days apart
worked_examples.narrative: The earlier commitment wins, so the Transfer as a whole is committed for the eighteenth of September.

records.name: The deadline of a Transfer shipping all at once
records.purpose: Gives the date by which a Transfer is committed when every one of its goods must leave together, which is the latest deadline among its moves.

operands.name: deadlines of the non-cancelled moves that have one
operands.constraints: moves without a deadline do not compete

operands.name: shipping policy
operands.unit_or_currency: as soon as possible, or all at once
operands.constraints: must be all at once for this variant

preconditions.condition: At least one non-cancelled move carries a deadline.
preconditions.otherwise: The Transfer's deadline is empty.

procedure: Take the deadlines of the Transfer's non-cancelled moves that have one.
Take their maximum.
Leave the Transfer's deadline empty when no move carries one.
records.formula: deadline = maximum( the deadlines of the non-cancelled moves that have one ) , when the shipping policy is all at once

rounding.what: Nothing; the maximum is taken over instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: deadline of the Transfer
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Transfer and compared against its scheduled date to raise the deadline issue indicator.

edge_cases.case: No move carries a deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The Transfer's deadline is empty.

edge_cases.case: A cancelled move carries a deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not compete.

edge_cases.case: The latest deadline is also the latest scheduled date.
edge_cases.outcome: The two figures coincide and no deadline issue arises.

worked_examples.description: The same two moves under the all-at-once policy
worked_examples.narrative: The later commitment wins, because the whole Transfer must leave together and cannot be complete before its latest part is due.

records.name: The deadline issue indicator of a Transfer
records.purpose: Marks a Transfer whose commitment falls before the date it is actually planned for, which is the signal that the promise cannot be kept as planned.

operands.name: deadline of the Transfer
operands.source: the deadline calculation for the Transfer's shipping policy
operands.constraints: the indicator is false when it is empty

operands.name: scheduled date of the Transfer
operands.source: the scheduled date calculation for the Transfer's shipping policy
operands.constraints: always present

preconditions.condition: The Transfer carries a deadline.
preconditions.otherwise: The indicator is false, because there is no commitment to miss.

procedure: Check that the Transfer carries a deadline.
Compare the deadline against the scheduled date.
Set the indicator when the deadline is strictly earlier than the scheduled date, and leave it unset otherwise.
records.formula: deadline issue = ( the deadline exists ) and ( deadline < scheduled date )

rounding.what: Nothing; the comparison is on instants.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: deadline issue indicator
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the Transfer as the warning that the commitment falls before the plan.

edge_cases.case: The deadline is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The indicator is false whatever the scheduled date.

edge_cases.case: The deadline equals the scheduled date.
edge_cases.outcome: The indicator is false, because the comparison is strictly earlier.

edge_cases.case: The scheduled date moves later because a move was delayed.
edge_cases.outcome: The indicator can turn true without the deadline changing at all.

worked_examples.description: A delivery committed for the eighteenth but planned for the twentieth
worked_examples.narrative: The commitment falls two days before the plan, so the indicator is set.

worked_examples.description: The same delivery once the plan is brought forward
worked_examples.narrative: The plan is now earlier than the commitment, so the indicator is unset.

records.name: The reservation date of a normal move
records.purpose: Gives the day from which a move of ordinary priority may be reserved automatically, computed backwards from its scheduled date by the Operation Type's ordinary day count.

operands.name: date of the move
operands.constraints: only its date part is used

operands.name: days before the scheduled date
operands.source: the Operation Type's ordinary day count
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: priority of the move
operands.constraints: must be normal for this variant

operands.name: status of the move
operands.constraints: the date is computed only for draft, waiting, waiting another move and partially available

preconditions.condition: The Operation Type reserves before the scheduled date.
preconditions.otherwise: The reservation date is empty for a manual policy, or is stamped as today at confirmation for the policy that reserves at confirmation.

preconditions.condition: The move's status is draft, waiting, waiting another move or partially available.
preconditions.otherwise: The date is not computed.

procedure: Take the date part of the move's date, discarding the time.
Subtract the Operation Type's ordinary day count.
Store the result as the move's reservation date.
Leave the reservation date empty when the Operation Type reserves manually.
Stamp today as the reservation date at confirmation time when the Operation Type reserves at confirmation.
records.formula: reservation date = the date part of the move's date − the ordinary count of days before the scheduled date

rounding.what: The truncation of the move's date to its date part.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: Before the subtraction.

result.name: reservation date of the move
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the move and read by the daily reservation job and by the re-reservation search.

edge_cases.case: The Operation Type reserves manually.
edge_cases.outcome: The reservation date is empty and the move is only reserved when a person asks.

edge_cases.case: The Operation Type reserves at confirmation.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is stamped at confirmation time rather than a date computed backwards.

edge_cases.case: The Operation Type's reservation method is changed to reserve before the scheduled date.
edge_cases.outcome: The reservation date of every open move of the type is recomputed, reading the new day counts from the same write when they are present.

edge_cases.case: The move becomes assigned, done or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The reservation date is no longer recomputed; a change of the method to anything else clears it for the moves that are not assigned, done or cancelled.

worked_examples.description: A move scheduled for the twentieth with an ordinary count of three days
worked_examples.narrative: The time is discarded and three days are subtracted, so the move becomes eligible for automatic reservation on the seventeenth of September.

related_rules: business-rules.md write-time behaviour on an Operation Type, points 3 and 4

records.name: The reservation date of an urgent move
records.purpose: Gives the day from which an urgent move may be reserved automatically, computed backwards from its scheduled date by the Operation Type's urgent day count rather than its ordinary one.

operands.name: date of the move
operands.constraints: only its date part is used

operands.name: days before the scheduled date for an urgent move
operands.source: the Operation Type's urgent day count
operands.constraints: zero or more

operands.name: priority of the move
operands.constraints: must be urgent for this variant

operands.name: status of the move
operands.constraints: the date is computed only for draft, waiting, waiting another move and partially available

preconditions.condition: The Operation Type reserves before the scheduled date.
preconditions.otherwise: The reservation date is empty for a manual policy, or is stamped as today at confirmation for the policy that reserves at confirmation.

preconditions.condition: The move's priority is urgent.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary day count applies.

procedure: Take the date part of the move's date, discarding the time.
Subtract the Operation Type's urgent day count.
Store the result as the move's reservation date.
records.formula: reservation date = the date part of the move's date − the urgent count of days before the scheduled date

rounding.what: The truncation of the move's date to its date part.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: Before the subtraction.

result.name: reservation date of the move
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the move and read by the daily reservation job and by the re-reservation search.

edge_cases.case: The urgent day count is larger than the ordinary one.

edge_cases.case: The urgent day count is zero.

records.name: Eligibility of a move for automatic reservation
records.purpose: States the three ways a move becomes eligible for the automatic reservation job, so that a rebuild reserves the same moves on the same day.

operands.name: reservation bypass of the move
operands.source: the source Location's usage and the product's storability
operands.constraints: a bypassing move is always eligible

operands.name: reservation policy of the Operation Type
operands.unit_or_currency: manual, at confirmation, or before the scheduled date
operands.constraints: the policy that reserves at confirmation makes the move eligible

operands.name: reservation date of the move
operands.constraints: must be on or before today for the third way

operands.name: today
operands.constraints: compared against the reservation date

preconditions.condition: The move is in a status that can still be reserved.
preconditions.otherwise: The reservation pass skips it whatever its eligibility.

procedure: Declare the move eligible when it bypasses reservation.
Declare it eligible when its Operation Type reserves at confirmation.
Declare it eligible when it has a reservation date that is on or before today.
Declare it not eligible in every other case.
records.formula: eligible = ( the move bypasses reservation ) or ( its Operation Type reserves at confirmation ) or ( its reservation date exists and is on or before today )

rounding.what: The comparison of the reservation date against today, made on whole days.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: Once per move, when the job builds its candidate set.

result.name: eligibility of the move for automatic reservation
result.stored_or_displayed: Used by the daily reservation job and by the re-reservation search to build their candidate sets.

edge_cases.case: The Operation Type reserves manually.
edge_cases.outcome: The reservation date is empty and the move is only eligible if it bypasses reservation.

edge_cases.case: The reservation date is exactly today.
edge_cases.outcome: The move is eligible, because the comparison is on or before.

edge_cases.case: The move bypasses reservation.
edge_cases.outcome: It is always eligible, because there is nothing to promise and the lines can be created at once.

records.name: The date categories of the operation overview
records.purpose: Buckets a date into one of six named ranges around today, in the reading user's own time zone, which is how the operation overview counts the Transfers of each day.

operands.name: date to classify
operands.source: the scheduled date of a Transfer
operands.constraints: an empty date belongs to no category

operands.name: start of today
operands.source: midnight of the current day in the reading user's time zone, expressed in coordinated universal time
operands.constraints: the anchor of every boundary

preconditions.condition: The reading user's time zone is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The boundaries cannot be anchored and the buckets would differ between readers.

procedure: Take midnight of the current day in the reading user's time zone, expressed in coordinated universal time, and call it the start of today.
Define the start of yesterday as the start of today less one day.
Define the start of the first day, of the second day and of the third day as the start of today plus one, two and three days.
Classify a date earlier than the start of yesterday as the category for earlier dates.
Classify a date on or after the start of yesterday and earlier than the start of today as yesterday.
Classify a date on or after the start of today and earlier than the start of the first day as today.
Classify a date on or after the start of the first day and earlier than the start of the second day as the first day.
Classify a date on or after the start of the second day and earlier than the start of the third day as the second day.
Classify a date on or after the start of the third day as the category for later dates.
Give an empty date no category at all.
records.formula: start of yesterday = start of today − 1 day ; start of day one = start of today + 1 day ; start of day two = start of today + 2 days ; start of day three = start of today + 3 days ; the categories are the half-open ranges between those boundaries, with the stored values `before`, `yesterday`, `today`, `day_1`, `day_2` and `after`

rounding.what: The truncation of the current instant to midnight in the reader's time zone.
rounding.precision: Whole days in the reader's time zone.
rounding.method: Truncation to the start of the day.
rounding.step: Once, before the five boundaries are derived.

result.name: the category of the date
result.unit_or_currency: one of the six stored category values
result.stored_or_displayed: Used to bucket and count the Transfers of the operation overview graph.

edge_cases.case: The date falls exactly on a boundary.
edge_cases.outcome: It belongs to the later category, because every range is closed at its start and open at its end.

edge_cases.case: The date is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: It belongs to no category and is not counted.

edge_cases.case: Two readers are in different time zones.
edge_cases.outcome: Each sees the boundaries anchored on their own midnight, so a date near midnight may fall in different buckets for them.

worked_examples.narrative: The eighth is earlier than the start of yesterday and falls in the earlier bucket; the tenth is yesterday; the eleventh is today; the fourteenth is on or after the start of the third day and falls in the later bucket.

records.name: The next count date of a Location
records.purpose: Gives the day a Location is next due to be counted, from its counting frequency and the day it was last counted, and refuses a frequency that would push the date beyond the calendar.

operands.name: counting frequency
operands.constraints: must not be negative; a frequency of zero leaves the date empty

operands.name: last count date
operands.constraints: when absent the frequency is added to today

operands.name: today
operands.constraints: the anchor of both branches

operands.name: usage of the Location
operands.constraints: must be internal or transit

operands.name: company of the Location
operands.constraints: the date is empty when the Location has no company

preconditions.condition: The Location has a company, its usage is internal or transit, and its counting frequency is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The next count date is empty.

preconditions.condition: The arithmetic stays within the representable calendar.
preconditions.otherwise: The write fails with the message that the selected inventory frequency in days creates a date too far into the future.

procedure: Leave the date empty when the Location has no company, or its usage is neither internal nor transit, or its counting frequency is zero.
When the Location has a last count date, compute the days until the next count as the counting frequency less the whole number of days between the last count date and today.
When that figure is zero or negative, set the next count date to today plus one day.
Otherwise set it to the last count date plus the counting frequency in days.
When the Location has no last count date, set the next count date to today plus the counting frequency in days.
Fail with the message about a date too far into the future when the arithmetic overflows the calendar.
records.formula: days until next = counting frequency − ( today − last count date ) in whole days ; next count date = today + 1 day when days until next ≤ 0 ; = last count date + counting frequency days otherwise ; next count date = today + counting frequency days when there is no last count date

rounding.what: The difference between today and the last count date, taken in whole days.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: Once, when the days until the next count are computed.

result.name: next count date of the Location
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Location and read when a quantity record's own next count date is computed.

edge_cases.case: The Location is overdue.
edge_cases.outcome: The days until the next count are zero or negative and the date becomes tomorrow, so the count is scheduled at once rather than in the past.

edge_cases.case: The Location has never been counted.
edge_cases.outcome: The frequency is added to today.

edge_cases.case: The counting frequency is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is empty and the Location is never scheduled.

edge_cases.case: The counting frequency is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused with the message that the inventory frequency in days for a location must be non-negative.

edge_cases.case: The frequency pushes the date beyond the representable calendar.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused with the message about a date too far into the future.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: Thirty less the ten days since the last count gives twenty, which is positive, so the date is the first of September plus thirty days, that is the first of October.

worked_examples.description: The same Location counted forty days ago
worked_examples.narrative: The Location is ten days overdue, so the days until the next count are negative and the date becomes tomorrow, the twelfth of September.

records.name: The company's yearly count date
records.purpose: Gives the next occurrence of the company's annual inventory day, clamping the day of the month so that a date such as the twenty-ninth of February resolves in a year that does not have one.

operands.name: annual inventory month
operands.constraints: the yearly date is empty when the company names none

operands.name: annual inventory day
operands.constraints: raised to at least one and clamped to the last day of the chosen month

operands.name: today
operands.constraints: decides whether this year's occurrence has passed

operands.name: last day of the chosen month
operands.source: the calendar of the year being considered
operands.constraints: the clamp that handles a short month

preconditions.condition: The company names an annual inventory month.
preconditions.otherwise: The yearly date is empty and only the Location's own next count date applies.

procedure: Take the greater of the company's annual inventory day and one, and then the smaller of that figure and the last day of the chosen month in the current year, giving the day of the month.
Build the candidate date from the current year, the chosen month and that day.
When the candidate is on or before today, recompute the day with the last day of the chosen month in the next year and build the candidate from the next year instead.
Return the candidate.
records.formula: day = minimum( maximum( annual inventory day , 1 ) , the last day of the chosen month in the current year ) ; candidate = ( current year , chosen month , day ) ; when candidate ≤ today: day = minimum( maximum( annual inventory day , 1 ) , the last day of the chosen month in the next year ) and candidate = ( next year , chosen month , day )

rounding.what: The clamping of the day of the month at both ends.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.method: The greater of the configured day and one, then the smaller of that and the last day of the month.
rounding.step: Once per candidate year, before the date is built.

result.name: the company's yearly count date
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the next count date of a quantity record.

edge_cases.case: The configured day is the twenty-ninth of February and the year is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The clamp gives the twenty-eighth, which is why the clamping is applied again in the second branch.

edge_cases.case: The candidate falls on today.
edge_cases.outcome: It is pushed to next year, because the comparison is on or before.

edge_cases.case: The configured day is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: It is raised to one.

edge_cases.case: The company names no annual inventory month.
edge_cases.outcome: The yearly date is empty.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The thirty-first of December exists in the current year and falls after today, so it stands as the yearly date.

worked_examples.description: A company whose annual inventory is the twenty-ninth of February, in a year that is not a leap year
worked_examples.narrative: The current year has no twenty-ninth of February, so the clamp gives the twenty-eighth; that date has already passed, so the second branch runs and clamps again for the next year, giving the twenty-eighth of February of the following year.

records.name: The next count date of a quantity record
records.purpose: Gives the day a Stock Quantity record is next due to be counted, combining the Location's own cycle with the company's annual inventory date.

operands.name: usage of the record's Location
operands.constraints: must be internal or transit

operands.name: next count date of the Location
operands.source: the Location's own next count date
operands.constraints: competes with the yearly date

operands.name: company's yearly count date
operands.source: the company's yearly count date calculation
operands.constraints: competes with the Location's date

preconditions.condition: The Location's usage is internal or transit.
preconditions.otherwise: The record's next count date is empty.

procedure: Leave the date empty when the Location's usage is neither internal nor transit.
Compute the company's yearly count date when the company names an annual inventory month.
When the Location has its own next count date, take the smaller of that date and the company's yearly date, or that date alone when the company has no yearly date.
Otherwise take the company's yearly date, or leave the date empty when there is none.
Write the result on the record, at creation and after each application of a count.
records.formula: record next count date = minimum( the Location's next count date , the company's yearly date ) when both exist ; = the Location's next count date when only that exists ; = the company's yearly date when only that exists ; = empty when neither does

rounding.what: Nothing beyond the whole-day clamping inherited from the two inputs.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.method: The earlier of the two dates.
rounding.step: Once, when the record is created and after each application of a count.

result.name: next count date of the Stock Quantity record
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the record and used to schedule the counting work.

edge_cases.case: The Location has no cycle and the company has no annual inventory.
edge_cases.outcome: The record's date is empty and no count is scheduled.

edge_cases.case: The Location's cycle falls after the annual date.
edge_cases.outcome: The annual date wins, because the earlier of the two is taken.

edge_cases.case: The Location's usage is customer, vendor, production, inventory loss or virtual.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is empty whatever the two inputs say.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The Location's own cycle falls on the first of October, which is earlier than the annual date of the thirty-first of December, so the earlier of the two is written on the record.

worked_examples.description: A Location with no cycle in a company with an annual inventory
worked_examples.narrative: Only the annual date exists, so it is written on the record.

records.name: The inventory difference of a counted record
records.purpose: Gives the quantity a count would add to or remove from a Stock Quantity record, which becomes the demand of the adjustment move when the count is applied.

operands.name: counted quantity
operands.source: the counted field of the record
operands.constraints: meaningful only when the counted flag is set

operands.name: on-hand quantity
operands.source: the on-hand field of the record
operands.constraints: may be negative

operands.name: counted flag
operands.constraints: the difference is zero when it is not set

preconditions.condition: The counted flag is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The difference is zero, so a record nobody has counted proposes no correction.

procedure: Read the counted flag; when it is not set, the difference is zero.
Otherwise subtract the on-hand quantity from the counted quantity.
Store the difference, which is what makes the outdated test possible afterwards.
records.formula: inventory difference = counted quantity − on-hand quantity , when the counted flag is set ; = 0 , otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the subtraction is exact.
rounding.precision: Not applicable to the difference itself.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: inventory difference
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the record, displayed in the counting screens and used as the demand of the adjustment move.

edge_cases.case: The count matches the on-hand quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero; when the application comes from the product's own quantity field, no move is created at all.

edge_cases.case: The count is below the on-hand quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is negative and the adjustment move goes from the record's Location to the inventory-loss Location.

edge_cases.case: The on-hand quantity is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is larger than the counted quantity, which is correct because the count must bring the record up from below zero.

worked_examples.description: A count of five on a record holding six
worked_examples.narrative: The count is one below the recorded figure, so the difference is minus one and one unit will move from the Location to the inventory-loss Location.

worked_examples.description: A record nobody has counted
worked_examples.narrative: The flag is not set, so the difference is zero and the record proposes no correction.

records.name: The outdated indicator of a counted record
records.purpose: Detects that the on-hand quantity has moved since a count was typed, which is what opens the conflict screen instead of silently applying a stale figure.

operands.name: counted quantity
operands.constraints: typed by a person

operands.name: stored inventory difference
operands.constraints: stored when the count was typed

operands.name: current on-hand quantity
operands.constraints: may have moved since

operands.name: counted flag
operands.constraints: the indicator is false when it is not set

preconditions.condition: The counted flag is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The indicator is false, because there is no count to be outdated.

preconditions.condition: The inventory difference is stored rather than recomputed.
preconditions.otherwise: The subtraction could not recover the on-hand quantity as it stood when the count was entered.

procedure: Read the counted flag; when it is not set, the indicator is false.
Subtract the stored inventory difference from the counted quantity, which recovers the on-hand quantity as it stood when the count was entered.
Compare that figure with the current on-hand quantity at the product unit's rounding step.
Set the indicator when the two differ.
records.formula: outdated = the counted flag is set and comparison( counted quantity − stored inventory difference , current on-hand quantity , product unit ) ≠ 0

rounding.what: The comparison of the recovered on-hand quantity against the current one.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit.
rounding.method: Comparison at the step; the subtraction is exact.
rounding.step: Once, after the subtraction.

result.name: outdated indicator
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the record and used to decide whether the conflict screen opens.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has moved since the count was typed.
edge_cases.outcome: The recovered figure equals the current one and the indicator is false.

edge_cases.case: A delivery has taken goods since the count was typed.
edge_cases.outcome: The two figures differ and the indicator is true, which opens the conflict screen at the next application.

edge_cases.case: The movement is smaller than the product unit's rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison at the step returns zero and the indicator stays false.

worked_examples.description: A count of five typed when the record held six, applied while it still holds six
worked_examples.narrative: Five less minus one is six, which equals the current figure, so the count is still current.

worked_examples.description: The same count applied after two units have been delivered
worked_examples.narrative: The record held six when the count was typed but holds four now, so the count is outdated and the conflict screen opens.

records.name: Applying the counted quantities
records.purpose: Turns the differences of a set of counted records into completed adjustment moves, in the right direction against the inventory-loss Location, and resets the counting fields afterwards.

operands.name: counted records
operands.source: the counting screen or an import
operands.constraints: every one is marked as counted first

operands.name: inventory difference of each record
operands.constraints: its sign decides the direction of the move

operands.name: inventory-loss Location
operands.source: the product's own inventory-loss Location in the record's company, else the company-level default for that field
operands.constraints: resolved per record

operands.name: adjustment reference
operands.source: the calling context, when it supplies one
operands.constraints: optional; stamped on the created moves

operands.name: explicit date
operands.source: the calling context, when it supplies one
operands.constraints: optional; written as the date of the created moves

preconditions.condition: The counting-mode context is active and the acting user is in the inventory user group.
preconditions.otherwise: The counted-quantity write is ignored entirely rather than refused.

preconditions.condition: No record of the set is outdated, or the person has answered the conflict screen.
preconditions.otherwise: The conflict screen opens instead of applying.

procedure: Mark every record of the set as counted.
Resolve the inventory-loss Location per record: the product's own inventory-loss Location in the record's company, and, when the product names none, the company-level default for that field.
Skip a record when the application comes from the product's own quantity field and its difference is zero.
When the difference is strictly positive, build a move of that difference from the inventory-loss Location to the record's Location, with the record's container as the destination container.
When it is not, build a move of the absolute difference from the record's Location to the inventory-loss Location, with the record's container as the source container.

Give each move the product, the product unit, the difference as demand, the company, the confirmed status, the owner as owner restriction, the adjustment flag, the picked flag, and one detail line carrying the same quantity, Locations, lot, containers and owner.
Stamp the adjustment reference on the move when the calling context supplies one.
Create all the moves and complete them with destination containers ignored.
Write the supplied date as the date of the created moves when one was supplied.
Trigger the re-reservation search from those moves.
Stamp today's date as the last-count date of every Location involved.
Recompute each record's next count date.
Clear the counted quantity, the difference, the counted flag and the assignee on every record.
records.formula: a move of the difference is built from the inventory-loss Location to the record's Location when the difference > 0 ; a move of the absolute difference is built from the record's Location to the inventory-loss Location otherwise ; the demand and the single detail line both carry that quantity in the product unit

rounding.what: The sign test of the difference; the moves themselves carry the difference unrounded in the product unit.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit for the sign test.
rounding.step: Once per record, before the direction is chosen.

result.name: the completed adjustment moves and the reset counting fields
result.stored_or_displayed: The moves and their lines are stored and completed; the counting fields of the records are cleared.

edge_cases.case: The difference is exactly zero and the application comes from the product's own quantity field.
edge_cases.outcome: No move is created at all for that record.

edge_cases.case: The difference is exactly zero and the application comes from the counting screen.
edge_cases.outcome: A move of zero is built and completed, because an adjustment move survives the pruning even with a zero processed quantity.

edge_cases.case: An inventory manager deletes a record instead of counting it.
edge_cases.outcome: The deletion is replaced by an adjustment to zero, so the disappearance is recorded as moves.

edge_cases.case: The record sits in an inventory-loss Location.
edge_cases.outcome: Typing a counted quantity there is refused with the warning that inventory loss quantities may not be modified.

edge_cases.case: Destination containers are ignored at the completion.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither the container history snapshots nor the application of the destination containers runs.

worked_examples.description: A count of five on a record holding six, applied from the counting screen
worked_examples.narrative: The difference is minus one, so one unit moves from the stock Location to the inventory-loss Location; the move completes at once and the record is left holding five with its counting fields cleared.

worked_examples.description: A count of eight on a record holding six
worked_examples.narrative: The difference is positive, so two units move from the inventory-loss Location into the stock Location and the record is left holding eight.
