records.name: Walking upstream from a detail line
records.purpose: Collects the completed lines that brought the same lot into the Location a line took it from, following explicit links for a chained move and matching heuristically for an unchained one.

operands.name: starting lines
operands.unit_or_currency: a list of completed detail lines
operands.source: the root set or the node being unfolded
operands.constraints: seed both the queue and the set of seen lines

operands.name: originating moves of the line's move
operands.constraints: their completed lines of the same lot are the chained candidates

operands.name: source Location usage of the line
operands.constraints: must be internal or transit for the unchained case

operands.name: date of the line
operands.constraints: an unchained candidate must be dated on or before it

operands.name: set of seen lines
operands.constraints: prevents cycles

preconditions.condition: The starting lines are completed.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is walked, because the report only shows completed lines.

procedure: Seed the set of seen lines and the queue with the starting lines.
Pop a line from the queue.
When the line's move has originating moves, take as candidates the completed detail lines of those originating moves whose lot equals this line's lot, minus the lines already seen.

Otherwise, when the line's source Location's usage is internal or transit, take as candidates the completed detail lines with the same product, the same lot, a destination Location exactly equal to this line's source Location, a date on or before this line's date, and an identifier not already seen.
Otherwise, the goods having come from outside, take no candidate at all and stop for this line.
When the walk is unfolding one specific line, descend only into the candidates when that line is among them.
Add the candidates to the set of seen lines and continue with the queue.
Return the set of seen lines minus the starting lines.
records.formula: candidates(line) = the completed detail lines of the originating moves whose lot equals this line's lot , for a chained move ; = the completed detail lines with the same product , the same lot , a destination Location exactly equal to this line's source Location and a date on or before this line's date , for an unchained move whose source usage is internal or transit ; = none otherwise ; the result is the set of seen lines minus the starting lines

rounding.what: Nothing; the walk compares Locations, lots, dates and identifiers.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the lines that brought the lot into the Location
result.unit_or_currency: a list of completed detail lines
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the next level of the tree.

edge_cases.case: The line's source Location has vendor usage.
edge_cases.outcome: There are no candidates, because the goods came from outside the company.

edge_cases.case: A candidate has already been seen.
edge_cases.outcome: It is skipped, which is what prevents a cycle.

edge_cases.case: The move is chained.
edge_cases.outcome: The explicit links are followed rather than the heuristic match, which is the deliberate asymmetry of the walk.

edge_cases.case: An unchained candidate is dated after the line.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, because goods cannot have arrived after they left.

worked_examples.description: A delivery line of lot A taken from a shelf that a receipt filled

candidates_returned: the line of the fifth of September
excluded: the line of the twentieth of September, dated after the starting line

worked_examples.narrative: The move is unchained and its source Location is internal, so the heuristic match applies; only the earlier arrival at exactly that shelf qualifies.

records.name: What each node of the traceability tree shows
records.purpose: Fixes the seven columns of a traceability node and the colour marker that goes with it, including the rounding of the quantity it displays.

operands.name: Transfer of the line
operands.constraints: its reference is the first choice for the reference column

operands.name: adjustment flag and Scrap link of the move
operands.unit_or_currency: a yes or no flag and a Scrap, or nothing
operands.constraints: provide the fallback references

operands.name: date of the move
operands.constraints: formatted for the reader without a time zone shift

operands.name: quantity of the line
operands.constraints: converted into the product unit and rendered at the Product Unit precision

operands.name: usages of the two Locations
operands.source: the line's source and destination Locations
operands.constraints: decide the colour marker

preconditions.condition: The line is completed.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not a node of the tree.

procedure: Show as the reference the Transfer's reference when the line has one; otherwise the literal text "Inventory Adjustment" when the move is an adjustment move; otherwise the Scrap's reference when the move's destination usage is inventory loss and it belongs to a Scrap; otherwise nothing; and carry with it the model and identifier the node links to, so that the node can be opened.
Show the product's display name.
Show the move's date, formatted for the reader without a time zone shift.
Show the lot's name.
Show, in the from column, the Transfer's contact name for a receipt and the source Location's display name otherwise.
Show, in the to column, the Transfer's contact name for a delivery and the destination Location's display name otherwise.
Show the line's quantity converted into the product unit, rounding half away from zero, rendered at the `Product Unit` precision, followed by the product unit's name.
Mark the node as internal when both Locations have internal usage, as incoming when only the destination has, and as outgoing in every other case.
records.formula: displayed quantity = convert( line quantity , line unit , product unit , half away from zero ) , rendered at the `Product Unit` decimal precision , followed by the product unit's name ; the colour marker is internal when both usages are internal , incoming when only the destination usage is , and outgoing otherwise

rounding.what: The displayed quantity.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit for the conversion and the `Product Unit` decimal precision for the rendering.
rounding.step: Once per node, at display time.

result.name: the seven columns and the colour marker of the node
result.unit_or_currency: texts, a date and a quantity in the product unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the traceability report and rendered on its printed form.

edge_cases.case: The move is an adjustment move with no Transfer.
edge_cases.outcome: The reference column shows the literal text for an inventory adjustment.

edge_cases.case: The move belongs to a Scrap and its destination has inventory-loss usage.
edge_cases.outcome: The reference column shows the Scrap's reference.

edge_cases.case: The line belongs to a receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The from column shows the Transfer's contact name rather than the source Location.

edge_cases.case: Both Locations are internal.
edge_cases.outcome: The node is marked as internal, which colours it as an internal displacement.

edge_cases.case: The date shown is the move's, not the line's.
edge_cases.outcome: Two lines of one move therefore show the same date even when their own dates differ.

worked_examples.description: A delivery line of four units
worked_examples.narrative: The Transfer's reference is shown, the to column shows the contact because the Operation Type is a delivery, and the quantity is rendered at two digits followed by the product unit's name.

records.name: Whether a traceability node can be unfolded
records.purpose: Decides whether a node offers a further level, which is either a production genealogy or an upstream walk that finds something.

operands.name: consumed lines recorded by the production genealogy
operands.constraints: their presence alone makes the node unfoldable

operands.name: record the report was opened from
operands.unit_or_currency: a Lot, a detail line, a Transfer or a manufacturing order
operands.constraints: a report opened from a Lot does not use the second test

operands.name: lot of the line
operands.constraints: required for the second test

operands.name: result of the upstream walk
operands.constraints: at least one line is required

preconditions.condition: The node is a completed detail line.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not part of the tree at all.

procedure: Declare the node unfoldable when the production genealogy records consumed lines for it.
Otherwise declare it unfoldable when the report was not opened from a Lot, the line carries a lot, and the upstream walk from that line finds at least one line.
Declare it not unfoldable in every other case.
records.formula: unfoldable = ( the production genealogy records consumed lines for the node ) or ( the report was not opened from a Lot and the line carries a lot and the upstream walk finds at least one line )

rounding.what: Nothing; the decision counts lines.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the unfoldability of the node
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the marker that a node can be opened.

edge_cases.case: The report was opened from a Lot.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the genealogy test applies, because the whole history of that lot is already the root set.

edge_cases.case: The line carries no lot.
edge_cases.outcome: The second test cannot apply and only a genealogy makes the node unfoldable.

edge_cases.case: The upstream walk finds nothing.
edge_cases.outcome: The node is a leaf, which is what happens when the goods came from outside the company.

worked_examples.description: A delivery node of a lot received earlier, in a report opened from a Transfer
worked_examples.narrative: The report was not opened from a Lot, the line carries a lot and the walk finds the receipt that brought it, so the node can be unfolded.

worked_examples.description: The same node in a report opened from the Lot itself
worked_examples.narrative: The second test does not apply to a report opened from a Lot, and there is no genealogy, so the node is a leaf.

records.name: Ordering and printing the traceability tree
records.purpose: Fixes the order of the nodes of one level and what a printed traceability report contains.

operands.name: nodes of one level
operands.unit_or_currency: a list of completed detail lines
operands.source: the root set or an unfolded level
operands.constraints: sorted by date descending

operands.name: unfolded state of the tree
operands.constraints: only the opened nodes are printed

operands.name: record the report was opened from
operands.constraints: its reference becomes the document title and its company the document's company

preconditions.condition: The report has been opened and, for printing, the person has unfolded what they want to see.
preconditions.otherwise: The printed document shows only the first level.

procedure: Sort the nodes of one level by date descending.
When printing, render exactly the nodes the person has currently unfolded.
Print in landscape.
Use the reference of the record the report was opened from as the document title.
Use that record's company as the document's company when it has one.
records.formula: the nodes of one level are ordered by date descending ; the printed document contains exactly the currently unfolded nodes , in landscape , titled with the reference of the record the report was opened from

rounding.what: Nothing; the ordering compares dates.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the ordered nodes and the printed document
result.unit_or_currency: a list of nodes and a document
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the report and rendered on its printed form.

edge_cases.case: Two nodes share a date.
edge_cases.outcome: Their relative order is whatever the underlying selection produced, the sort being on the date alone.

edge_cases.case: The person has unfolded nothing.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the first level is printed.

edge_cases.case: The record the report was opened from has no company.
edge_cases.outcome: The document carries no company.

worked_examples.description: A level of three nodes
worked_examples.narrative: The most recent node is shown first, because the level is sorted by date descending.

records.name: Discovering which deliveries carried a lot
records.purpose: Finds the outgoing Transfers that finally carried a lot, following the production genealogy so that a lot consumed to make another lot is credited with the deliveries of its descendants.

operands.name: lots being asked about
operands.constraints: seed the queue

operands.name: completed outgoing detail lines of a lot
operands.source: the lines whose Operation Type kind is a delivery, or whose move's Operation Type kind is a delivery, or which have produced lines
operands.constraints: the definition of outgoing here

operands.name: produced lines of a line
operands.constraints: their lots become children of the lot

operands.name: Transfers of the leaf lines
operands.constraints: the initial Transfer set of each lot

preconditions.condition: The lines considered are completed.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is discovered, because only completed lines carry goods.

procedure: Seed a queue with the lots being asked about.

While the queue is not empty, search the completed detail lines of those lots that are outgoing, meaning the line's Operation Type kind is a delivery, or its move's Operation Type kind is a delivery, or the line has produced lines.
For a line with produced lines, record each produced lot as a child of this lot and enqueue the children not yet seen.
For a line without produced lines, record the line as a leaf line of this lot.
Initialise each lot's Transfer set with the Transfers of its leaf lines and mark those lots for propagation.
Repeatedly take a marked lot and push its Transfer set up to each of its parents; whenever a parent gains a Transfer it did not have, mark the parent for propagation too.
Return each lot's accumulated Transfer set.
Take the contacts of a lot as the contacts of those Transfers, ordered by completion date descending.
records.formula: Transfer set(lot) = the Transfers of the lot's own leaf lines , united with the Transfer sets of every lot produced from it , transitively

rounding.what: Nothing; the discovery unites sets of Transfers.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the Transfers that carried the lot and their contacts
result.unit_or_currency: a set of Transfers and a list of Contacts
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the Lot as the deliveries and the contacts that received it.

edge_cases.case: A lot was consumed to produce another lot.
edge_cases.outcome: The produced lot becomes its child and the parent inherits the child's Transfers.

edge_cases.case: A lot was never delivered.
edge_cases.outcome: Its Transfer set is empty.

edge_cases.case: A child lot is reached twice.
edge_cases.outcome: It is enqueued only once, because the walk keeps the lots it has already seen.

edge_cases.case: A parent gains no new Transfer from a child.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not marked again, which is what terminates the propagation.

worked_examples.description: A component lot consumed to make a finished lot that was then delivered twice
worked_examples.narrative: The component lot has no delivery of its own, but its child was delivered twice, so both Transfers propagate up and the component lot is credited with them.

records.name: Generating a series of names from a first name
records.purpose: Produces a run of serial numbers or lot names from one typed name, by finding the digits inside it and incrementing them while keeping the padding and everything around them.

operands.name: first name
operands.source: the person typing it, or the most recently created Lot of the product
operands.constraints: a digit is appended when it holds none

operands.name: count
operands.constraints: must be greater than zero

operands.name: last run of digits in the name
operands.constraints: its length is the padding and its value the starting number

operands.name: prefix and suffix
operands.source: the first name split on that digit run
operands.constraints: the prefix re-joins every part except the last with the digit run itself

preconditions.condition: The first name contains at least one run of digits.
preconditions.otherwise: The digit zero is appended to the name and the search starts again.

procedure: Find every run of digits in the first name; when there is none, append the digit zero to the name and start again.
Take the last run of digits: its length is the padding and its value is the starting number.
Split the name on that exact digit run; the prefix is every part except the last, re-joined with the digit run itself, and the suffix is the last part.
Produce the requested count of names by adding the position to the starting number, padding the result with leading zeros to the padding length, and placing it between the prefix and the suffix.
records.formula: name(i) = prefix ‖ zero-padded( starting number + i , padding ) ‖ suffix , for i from 0 to count − 1

rounding.what: The zero padding of the incremented number to the length of the original digit run.
rounding.precision: The padding length, which is the number of digits of the last run.
rounding.method: Leading zeros are added until the padding length is reached.
rounding.step: Once per generated name.

result.name: the generated series of names
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as the typed names of the detail lines, and resolved into Lot records when the Operation Type allows using existing lots.

edge_cases.case: The name holds several runs of digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The last run is the one incremented, and the earlier runs stay in the prefix, so a name such as one carrying two numbered segments keeps its first segment.

edge_cases.case: The name holds no digit at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The digit zero is appended and the generation starts from that.

edge_cases.case: The incremented number needs more digits than the padding.
edge_cases.outcome: The number is written in full; the padding only adds leading zeros, it does not truncate.

edge_cases.case: The count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The generation on a move fails with the message that the number of serial numbers to generate must be greater than zero.

worked_examples.description: The first worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The last run of digits is five characters long and holds seven, so three names are produced by incrementing it while keeping the padding.

worked_examples.description: The second worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The name holds no digit, so a zero is appended and the two names are produced from that.

worked_examples.description: A name holding two runs of digits
worked_examples.narrative: The last run of five digits is the one incremented; the earlier runs stay inside the prefix, which is why the prefix is re-joined with the digit run itself.

records.name: The next serial number for a product
records.purpose: Proposes the serial number that follows the last one created for a product, by generating two names from the most recent one and returning the second.

operands.name: most recently created Lot of the product
operands.source: the Lots of that product belonging to the company or to no company
operands.constraints: the newest by creation

operands.name: name of that Lot
operands.constraints: the first name of the generation

operands.name: company
operands.constraints: the Lot must belong to it or to no company

preconditions.condition: At least one Lot of the product belongs to the company or to no company.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is returned.

procedure: Take the most recently created Lot of that product belonging to the company or to no company.
Generate two names from its name.
Return the second of the two.
Return nothing when there is no such Lot.
records.formula: next serial number = the second name of the two generated from the name of the most recently created Lot of that product belonging to the company or to no company

rounding.what: The zero padding inherited from the name generation.
rounding.precision: The padding length of the last digit run of the name.
rounding.step: Once, inside the generation.

result.name: the proposed next serial number
result.stored_or_displayed: Proposed in the screens that ask for a first serial number.

edge_cases.case: The product has no Lot at all.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is returned and the person types the first name themselves.

edge_cases.case: The most recent Lot's name holds no digit.
edge_cases.outcome: The generation appends a zero, so the proposal is that name followed by one.

edge_cases.case: A Lot of another company exists.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not considered, only the company's own Lots and the company-less pool being read.

worked_examples.description: A product whose most recent serial number is the seventh of a padded series
worked_examples.narrative: Two names are generated and the second is returned, so the proposal is the eighth of the series.

records.name: Generating serial numbers on a move
records.purpose: Fills a move with one detail line per generated serial number, resolving or creating the Lot records when the Operation Type allows using existing ones.

operands.name: count of names to generate
operands.source: the supplied figure, else the move's own serial-number count
operands.constraints: must be greater than zero

operands.name: first name
operands.source: the person or the next serial number of the product
operands.constraints: seeds the generation

operands.name: lot policy of the Operation Type
operands.constraints: using existing lots turns the typed names into Lot links

operands.name: generated entries
operands.unit_or_currency: a name and a quantity of one each
operands.constraints: one entry per name

preconditions.condition: The count is greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation fails with the message that the number of serial numbers to generate must be greater than zero.

preconditions.condition: A product is in context.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation fails with the message that no product was found to generate serial numbers or lots for.

procedure: Take the count from the supplied figure, or from the move's own serial-number count when none was supplied; fail when it is zero.
Generate the names and build one entry per name with a quantity of one.
When the Operation Type allows using existing lots, resolve or create the Lot records for those names now and replace the typed names by the Lot links.
Turn the entries into detail-line operations and write them onto the move.
records.formula: one entry of exactly one unit per generated name ; the count of entries = the count of names generated

rounding.what: The zero padding inherited from the name generation.
rounding.precision: The padding length of the last digit run of the first name.
rounding.step: Once per generated name.

result.name: the detail lines of the move, one per serial number
result.unit_or_currency: one unit of the product unit each
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the move; the move's processed quantity is recomputed from them.

edge_cases.case: The count is zero or absent.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation fails with the quoted message about the number of serial numbers to generate.

edge_cases.case: The Operation Type does not allow using existing lots.
edge_cases.outcome: The names stay as typed names on the lines and are resolved at completion.

edge_cases.case: A generated name already names an existing Lot.
edge_cases.outcome: That Lot is linked rather than a second one created, when the Operation Type allows using existing lots.

worked_examples.description: Generating three serial numbers on a receipt whose Operation Type uses existing lots
worked_examples.narrative: Three names are generated, each becomes an entry of one unit, the Lot records are resolved or created at once and three detail lines are written on the move.

related_rules: business-rules.md switch that forces the creation of Lot records

records.name: The quantity per lot when generating lots
records.purpose: Splits a total quantity into entries when lots rather than serial numbers are generated, where the requested number is the quantity carried by each entry rather than the number of entries.

operands.name: requested number
operands.source: the person, as the quantity per lot
operands.constraints: must be a positive value

operands.name: total quantity
operands.source: the move or the calling screen
operands.constraints: split into whole entries and a leftover

preconditions.condition: The requested number is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation fails with the message that the quantity per lot should always be a positive value.

procedure: Divide the total quantity by the requested number and take the integer part, giving the number of whole entries.
Subtract the whole entries multiplied by the requested number from the total quantity, giving the leftover.
Produce that many entries, each of the requested number of units.
Produce one further entry of the leftover when the leftover is not zero.
records.formula: whole lines = the integer part of ( quantity ÷ count ) ; leftover = quantity − whole lines × count ; the result is whole lines entries of count units each , plus one entry of leftover units when the leftover is not zero

rounding.what: The division, of which only the integer part is kept.
rounding.precision: Whole entries.
rounding.step: Once, before the leftover is computed.

result.name: the entries and their quantities
result.stored_or_displayed: Turned into detail-line operations and written onto the move.

edge_cases.case: The total quantity divides exactly by the requested number.
edge_cases.outcome: The leftover is zero and no extra entry is produced.

edge_cases.case: The requested number exceeds the total quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: No whole entry is produced and the single leftover entry carries the whole quantity.

edge_cases.case: The requested number is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation fails with the message that the quantity per lot should always be a positive value.

edge_cases.case: The requested number is read as a count of lots.
edge_cases.outcome: That is a misreading: the figure is the quantity per lot, not the number of lots.

worked_examples.description: Splitting twenty-five units into lots of ten
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-five divided by ten has an integer part of two, and twenty-five less twenty is five, so two entries of ten and one of five are produced.

worked_examples.description: Splitting twenty units into lots of ten
worked_examples.narrative: The division is exact, so the leftover is zero and only the two whole entries are produced.

records.name: Turning generated entries into detail-line operations
records.purpose: Writes the generated names and quantities onto the move, reusing the lines that carry no lot and putting away each new line while accounting for the goods the same operation is already sending to each Location.

operands.name: entries
operands.unit_or_currency: a name and a quantity each
operands.source: the name generation or the parsing of a pasted list
operands.constraints: consumed in order

operands.name: reusable detail lines
operands.source: the move's lines that have neither a Lot nor a typed name
operands.constraints: reused in order

operands.name: running tally per Location
operands.constraints: passed to put-away as the additional-quantity map

operands.name: origin line
operands.constraints: when supplied, its owner, source container and destination Location are copied

preconditions.condition: The move exists and carries a product and a source Location.
preconditions.otherwise: No line can be built.

procedure: Take the move's detail lines that have neither a Lot nor a typed name; they will be reused in order.
For each entry, when a reusable line is left, update it with the entry's values and add the entry's quantity to the running tally of the line's current destination Location.

Otherwise create a new line with the move's Transfer, source Location, product and product unit, together with the entry's values, and resolve its destination Location by put-away for the entry's quantity, passing the running tally as the additional-quantity map.
Add the entry's quantity to the tally of that Location.
When the caller supplied an origin line, copy its owner and source container onto the new lines and use its destination Location instead of running put-away.
records.formula: the number of new lines = the number of entries − the number of reusable lines , when that is positive ; the put-away of each new line is resolved with the running tally per Location as the additional-quantity map , so that the goods this operation is already sending to a Location count against its capacity

rounding.what: The comparisons inside the put-away that each new line runs.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit.
rounding.step: Once per new line, inside the put-away.

result.name: the created and updated detail lines
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the move.

edge_cases.case: There are more reusable lines than entries.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus reusable lines are left as they are by this routine.

edge_cases.case: An origin line is supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: Put-away is not run at all and the origin line's destination Location is used.

edge_cases.case: Two entries would fill the same shelf.
edge_cases.outcome: The running tally makes the second one see the first one's quantity as occupancy, so it may be directed elsewhere.

worked_examples.description: Three generated serial numbers on a move with one reusable line
worked_examples.narrative: The single reusable line takes the first name and its quantity joins the tally of its current destination; the other two names become new lines, each put away with the tally passed so that the goods already directed there count against the capacity.

related_rules: business-rules.md switch that excludes detail lines from the occupancy

records.name: Parsing a pasted list of lot names
records.purpose: Turns a block of text a person pasted into entries of a name and a quantity, accepting a quantity typed after the name and falling back to the whole line when it cannot be read.

operands.name: pasted text
operands.constraints: split on line breaks with the empty lines dropped

operands.name: separators
operands.unit_or_currency: the semicolon and the tabulation character
operands.constraints: a semicolon is replaced by a tabulation character before the split

operands.name: decimal separator
operands.constraints: both are accepted for a quantity

preconditions.condition: The pasted text holds at least one non-empty line.
preconditions.otherwise: No entry is produced.

procedure: Split the pasted text on line breaks and drop the empty lines.
For each line, start an entry with the whole line as the typed name and a quantity of one.
Replace every semicolon by a tabulation character and split the line on tabulation characters.
For each part after the first, try to convert it into field data: a part that is a plain number, with either a dot or a comma as its decimal separator, becomes the entry's quantity.
When a part converts, reduce the typed name to the first part.
When a part does not convert, keep the whole original line as the typed name and ignore the remaining parts.
records.formula: one entry per non-empty line ; the entry's typed name = the first part when a later part converts into field data , and the whole line otherwise ; the entry's quantity = the converted number when one was read , and one otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the number is read as it is written.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the parsed entries
result.unit_or_currency: a text and a quantity each
result.stored_or_displayed: Turned into detail-line operations and written onto the move.

edge_cases.case: A line holds only a name.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry carries that name with a quantity of one.

edge_cases.case: A line holds a name and a number separated by a semicolon.
edge_cases.outcome: The semicolon becomes a tabulation character, the number becomes the quantity and the name is reduced to the first part.

edge_cases.case: A line holds a name and a part that is not a number.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole original line is kept as the typed name and the remaining parts are ignored.

edge_cases.case: The number uses a comma as its decimal separator.
edge_cases.outcome: It is accepted, both separators being read.

worked_examples.description: Three pasted lines of different shapes
worked_examples.narrative: The first line yields a name and a quantity of five; the second holds a part that is not a number, so the whole line stays as the typed name with a quantity of one; the third uses a comma as its decimal separator and yields two and a half.

records.name: Advancing the lot numbering sequence of a product
records.purpose: Moves a product's lot numbering sequence forward by the number of names that were generated, allowing for the fact that the screen may already have consumed one number.

operands.name: next number of the sequence
operands.constraints: read before the adjustment

operands.name: increment of the sequence
operands.constraints: the step between two numbers

operands.name: count of names generated
operands.constraints: added to the first number

operands.name: first name
operands.constraints: compared against the sequence rendering of two candidate numbers

preconditions.condition: The names were generated from a first name and the product has a lot numbering sequence.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is advanced.

procedure: Compute the first number as the sequence's next number less its increment.
When the first name equals the sequence rendering of the first number, set the final number to the first number plus the count.
When the first name equals the sequence rendering of the first number plus the increment, set the final number to the first number plus the increment plus the count.
Otherwise set the final number to the first number.
When the final number differs from the first number, set the sequence's next number to the final number.
records.formula: first number = the sequence's next number − the increment ; final number = first number + count when the first name equals the sequence rendering of the first number ; = first number + increment + count when it equals the sequence rendering of the first number plus the increment ; = first number otherwise ; the sequence's next number becomes the final number when the two differ

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole numbers.
rounding.precision: Whole numbers.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the sequence's next number
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the product's lot numbering sequence.

edge_cases.case: The generation screen already drew one number before the names were generated.
edge_cases.outcome: The first name equals the rendering of the first number plus the increment, so the increment is added as well as the count.

edge_cases.case: The first name matches neither rendering.
edge_cases.outcome: The final number equals the first number and the sequence is not advanced at all, because the names did not come from it.

edge_cases.case: The final number equals the first number.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is written.

worked_examples.description: Three names generated from the sequence's own next number
worked_examples.narrative: The first number is seven, the first name matches its rendering, so the final number is seven plus three, that is ten, and the sequence is advanced to ten.

worked_examples.description: The same generation where the screen had already drawn one number
worked_examples.narrative: The first name matches the rendering of the first number plus the increment, so the increment is added as well and the sequence is advanced to eleven.

related_rules: business-rules.md permission check on writing the numbering sequence of an Operation Type

records.name: The company consistency check
records.purpose: Refuses any link between a record and a company-scoped record of another company, which is what keeps a movement, a document and their Locations, Lots and containers inside one company.

operands.name: company of the record being checked
operands.constraints: compared against the company of every company-scoped link

operands.name: company of each linked record
operands.source: the Locations, Operation Types, Lots, containers and contacts the record links to
operands.constraints: a link whose company is set and differs is refused

operands.name: company of a Stock Rule and of its Route
operands.constraints: must be equal when the Route has one

operands.name: company of a Lot and the Location it sits in
operands.constraints: the company may not change while the lot sits in a Location of another company

preconditions.condition: The record names a company.
preconditions.otherwise: Its links are unconstrained by this check, a record with no company belonging to the shared pool.

procedure: For every entity of the domain that names a company and links to company-scoped records, refuse a link to a record whose company is set and differs from the record's own company.
Require therefore that the Locations, Operation Types, Lots, containers and contacts referenced by a move, a detail line or a Transfer all belong to the same company or to no company.
Refuse a Stock Rule whose company differs from its Route's company when the Route has one, with the message naming the rule, its company and the route's company.
Apply the same equality from the Route side, with the same message.
Refuse a change of company on a Lot while it sits in a Location of another company.
Refuse any change of company at all on a Location, an Operation Type, a Warehouse and a Put-away Rule.
records.formula: a link is refused when the linked record's company is set and differs from the record's own company ; a Stock Rule's company must equal its Route's company whenever the Route has one

rounding.what: Nothing; the check compares companies.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the consistency verdict
result.stored_or_displayed: A refusal stops the operation with its quoted message.

edge_cases.case: A linked record has no company.
edge_cases.outcome: The link is accepted, because only a company that is set and differs is refused.

edge_cases.case: A Route has no company.
edge_cases.outcome: Its rules may name any company.

edge_cases.case: A Lot sits in a Location of another company.
edge_cases.outcome: Its own company may not be changed until it leaves.

edge_cases.case: A Location, Operation Type, Warehouse or Put-away Rule is given a different company.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused outright, with the message that changing the company of the record is forbidden at this point.

worked_examples.description: A move of one company pointing at a Location of another
worked_examples.narrative: The Location's company is set and differs from the move's, so the link is refused.

worked_examples.description: The same move pointing at a Location with no company
worked_examples.narrative: A Location with no company belongs to the shared pool and may be used by any company.

records.name: Resolving a Warehouse from a Location
records.purpose: Matches every Location to the Warehouse that owns it, by testing its materialised path against each Warehouse's view Location, which is what lets the daily quantity series tell an inter-warehouse movement from an internal one.

operands.name: materialised path of the Location
operands.constraints: always starts with its parent's path

operands.name: view Location of each Warehouse
operands.constraints: its identifier is looked for as a complete segment

operands.name: identifier of the view Location
operands.constraints: the segment being matched

preconditions.condition: The Location has a materialised path.
preconditions.otherwise: No Warehouse can be matched.

procedure: Take the Location's materialised path.
For each Warehouse, test whether the path contains the identifier of the Warehouse's view Location as a complete segment, or starts with it.
Return that Warehouse when the test holds.
Return no warehouse when no Warehouse matches.
records.formula: the Location belongs to a Warehouse when its materialised path contains the identifier of that Warehouse's view Location as a complete segment , or starts with it ; otherwise it resolves to no warehouse

rounding.what: Nothing; the match is on a path.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the Warehouse of the Location, or none
result.stored_or_displayed: Used by the daily quantity series and cached until the Location tree changes.

edge_cases.case: The Location is a customer or a vendor Location.
edge_cases.outcome: It matches no Warehouse and resolves to no warehouse, which is what makes a delivery a purely outgoing row.

edge_cases.case: The Location is the view Location itself.
edge_cases.outcome: Its path starts with that identifier, so it matches.

edge_cases.case: The Location tree changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The cached Warehouse of every Location is invalidated after the write.

edge_cases.case: A segment of the path merely contains the identifier's digits.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not match, because the identifier must appear as a complete segment.

worked_examples.description: A shelf three levels below a warehouse's view Location

expected_outputs.warehouse: the warehouse whose view Location has that identifier

worked_examples.narrative: The identifier appears as a complete segment of the path, so the shelf belongs to that warehouse.

worked_examples.description: A customer Location outside every warehouse
worked_examples.narrative: No warehouse view Location appears in the path, so the Location resolves to no warehouse.

records.name: Selecting the moves of the daily quantity series
records.purpose: Chooses which Stock Moves take part in the daily series that answers how much of a product a warehouse will hold on each day of a window around today.

operands.name: storability of the product
operands.constraints: only storable products take part

operands.name: source Warehouse and destination Warehouse of the move
operands.unit_or_currency: Warehouses, either of which may be absent
operands.source: the Warehouse resolution of the two Locations
operands.constraints: the two must differ

operands.name: demand in the product unit and processed quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the product unit and the line unit
operands.constraints: at least one must be non-zero

operands.name: status of the move
operands.constraints: neither draft nor cancelled

operands.name: horizon
operands.source: the system parameter `stock.report_stock_quantity_period`, the setting that fixes the number of months of the window, with a default of three
operands.constraints: the window runs from today less the horizon to today plus the horizon

preconditions.condition: The horizon is known from the system parameter or from its default of three months.
preconditions.otherwise: The window cannot be built.

procedure: Take the Stock Moves whose product is storable.
Require that the source Warehouse and the destination Warehouse differ, either of them possibly being absent.
Require that the demand in the product unit is non-zero, or that the processed quantity is non-zero.
Require that the status is neither draft nor cancelled.
Require that the status is not done, or that the date is on or after today less the horizon.

Resolve the destination Warehouse from the final Location when the move is not done and one is set, and from the intermediate destination Location otherwise; resolve it always from the intermediate destination Location once the move is done.
records.formula: a move is selected when its product is storable , its source Warehouse ≠ its destination Warehouse , its demand in the product unit ≠ 0 or its processed quantity ≠ 0 , its status is neither draft nor cancelled , and ( its status is not done or its date ≥ today − the horizon )

rounding.what: The tests of the demand and of the processed quantity against zero.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit.
rounding.step: Once per move.

result.name: the selected moves and their resolved Warehouses
result.stored_or_displayed: Held while the series is regenerated; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: A move stays inside one warehouse.
edge_cases.outcome: Its two Warehouses are equal and it is not selected, because it does not change what the warehouse holds.

edge_cases.case: A move is done and older than the window.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not selected, because its effect is already inside the current stock and no day of the window needs correcting.

edge_cases.case: A move that is not done carries a final Location.
edge_cases.outcome: Its destination Warehouse is resolved from that final Location, so a chain that has not run yet already points at the warehouse the goods are really going to.

edge_cases.case: The move is done.
edge_cases.outcome: Its destination Warehouse is always resolved from the intermediate destination Location.

worked_examples.description: The moves of the worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: Both moves cross the warehouse boundary and are neither draft nor cancelled; the done receipt is dated inside the window, so both are selected.

records.name: The processed quantity of a move expressed in the product unit for the daily series
records.purpose: Converts a move's processed quantity into the product unit using the factors of the two units directly, which is the figure the completed movements of the daily series are corrected by.

operands.name: processed quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the line unit of the move
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: factor of the line unit
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: factor of the product unit
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The two units belong to the same category of units of measure.
preconditions.otherwise: Their factors are not comparable and the conversion is meaningless.

procedure: Multiply the processed quantity by the factor of the line unit.
Divide the product by the factor of the product unit.
Use the result wherever the series needs the processed quantity in the product unit.
records.formula: processed quantity in the product unit = processed quantity × line unit factor ÷ product unit factor

rounding.what: Nothing; the multiplication and the division are carried at full precision.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step, the series being regenerated on every read rather than stored.

result.name: the processed quantity in the product unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Held while the series is regenerated; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is the product unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The two factors are equal and the figure is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The processed quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero and the move contributes no correction.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is larger than the product unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is larger than the processed quantity, in the ratio of the two factors.

worked_examples.description: A processed quantity of five in a unit of twelve product units
worked_examples.narrative: Five multiplied by twelve and divided by one gives sixty product units.

worked_examples.description: The done receipt of the worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The two units are the same, so the five units of the receipt stand as five in the product unit.

records.name: Duplicating a move for an inter-warehouse movement
records.purpose: Expands each selected move into two rows so that a movement between two warehouses appears as an outgoing movement of the one and an incoming movement of the other.

operands.name: demand in the product unit of the move
operands.constraints: carried to the duplicate only when the two Warehouses differ

operands.name: processed quantity and its figure in the product unit
operands.unit_or_currency: the line unit and the product unit
operands.constraints: carried to the duplicate only when both Warehouses exist and differ

operands.name: source Warehouse of the move
operands.source: the Warehouse resolution of the source Location
operands.constraints: kept on the original row and cleared on the duplicate

operands.name: destination Warehouse of the move
operands.source: the Warehouse resolution of the destination Location
operands.constraints: kept on the original row only under the condition below

preconditions.condition: The move has been selected for the series.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not expanded at all.

procedure: Give the original row the move's demand in the product unit, its processed quantity and its processed quantity in the product unit, and its source Warehouse.
Give the original row the move's destination Warehouse only when there is no source Warehouse, or no destination Warehouse, or the two are equal.
Give the duplicate row the move's demand in the product unit when the two Warehouses differ, and zero otherwise.
Give the duplicate row the move's processed quantity and its figure in the product unit when both Warehouses exist and differ, and zero otherwise.
Give the duplicate row no source Warehouse.
Give the duplicate row the move's destination Warehouse only when both Warehouses exist and they differ.
records.formula: original row: demand and processed figures as they stand , source Warehouse = the move's , destination Warehouse = the move's only when there is no source Warehouse , or no destination Warehouse , or the two are equal ; duplicate row: demand and processed figures carried only when the two Warehouses differ , source Warehouse = none , destination Warehouse = the move's only when both exist and differ

rounding.what: Nothing; the figures are copied.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the two expanded rows of the move
result.stored_or_displayed: Held while the series is regenerated; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The move is purely incoming, having no source Warehouse.
edge_cases.outcome: The original row keeps the destination Warehouse and the duplicate carries no figure, so one meaningful row survives.

edge_cases.case: The move is purely outgoing, having no destination Warehouse.
edge_cases.outcome: The original row carries the source Warehouse and no destination one, and the duplicate carries no figure.

edge_cases.case: The move runs between two different warehouses.
edge_cases.outcome: The original row carries only a source Warehouse and the duplicate only a destination Warehouse, so the goods leave one and arrive in the other.

edge_cases.case: The two Warehouses are equal.
edge_cases.outcome: The move was not selected at all, the selection requiring them to differ.

worked_examples.description: A resupply of twelve between two warehouses
worked_examples.narrative: The original row shows the goods leaving the first warehouse and the duplicate shows them arriving in the second.

worked_examples.description: The planned delivery of the worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The delivery leaves the warehouse for a customer, so the original row is the meaningful one and the duplicate carries nothing.

records.name: The forecasted receipt and delivery rows of the daily series
records.purpose: Emits one row per planned movement on the day it is planned for, signed so that a departure lowers the figure and an arrival raises it.

operands.name: demand in the product unit of an expanded row
operands.source: the expanded rows of the selected moves
operands.constraints: must be non-zero

operands.name: status of the move
operands.constraints: must not be done

operands.name: source Warehouse and destination Warehouse of the expanded row
operands.constraints: exactly one of them decides the direction

operands.name: date of the move
operands.constraints: truncated to the day

preconditions.condition: The expanded row's demand is non-zero and the move's status is not done.
preconditions.otherwise: No such row is emitted.

procedure: Take the expanded rows whose demand is non-zero and whose status is not done.
Mark the row as outgoing when a source Warehouse is set and no destination Warehouse is.
Mark it as incoming when a destination Warehouse is set and no source Warehouse is.
Take the move's date truncated to the day.
Take the negation of the demand in the product unit for an outgoing row and the demand itself for an incoming one.
Take the source Warehouse for an outgoing row and the destination Warehouse for an incoming one.
records.formula: state = outgoing when a source Warehouse is set and no destination Warehouse is , incoming when a destination Warehouse is set and no source Warehouse is ; date = the move's date truncated to the day ; quantity = − demand in the product unit for an outgoing row , + demand in the product unit for an incoming row ; warehouse = the source Warehouse for an outgoing row , the destination Warehouse for an incoming one

rounding.what: The truncation of the move's date to the day.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.method: Truncation to the start of the day.
rounding.step: Once per row.

result.name: one planned movement row per expanded row
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the daily quantity series; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The move is done.
edge_cases.outcome: No planned movement row is emitted for it, only a forecast correction.

edge_cases.case: The expanded row carries both Warehouses or neither.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither direction applies, which is why the expansion clears one of them on each row.

edge_cases.case: The demand is zero on the duplicate row.
edge_cases.outcome: No row is emitted for it.

worked_examples.description: The planned delivery of the worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The delivery leaves the warehouse on the twentieth of September, so a row of minus eight is emitted for that day.

records.name: The forecast rows built from the quantity records
records.purpose: Repeats the current stock on every day of the window, which is the baseline the movement corrections are applied to.

operands.name: Stock Quantity records
operands.source: the records whose Location is internal and belongs to a Warehouse, or is transit
operands.constraints: only those qualify

operands.name: on-hand quantity of each record
operands.constraints: carried onto every day

operands.name: company and Warehouse of each record
operands.constraints: carried onto every row

operands.name: window
operands.source: today less the horizon to today plus the horizon
operands.constraints: one row per calendar day

preconditions.condition: The record's Location is internal and belongs to a Warehouse, or is transit.
preconditions.otherwise: The record contributes no row.

procedure: For every day of the whole window and every qualifying Stock Quantity record, emit a row whose state is the forecast state.
Give the row that day, the record's on-hand quantity, its company and its Warehouse.
Repeat the current stock on every day of the window, leaving the corrections to the rows built from the movements.
records.formula: one forecast row per day of the window and per qualifying quantity record , carrying that day , the record's on-hand quantity , its company and its Warehouse

rounding.what: Nothing; the on-hand quantity is carried as it stands.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the baseline forecast rows
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the daily quantity series after aggregation; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The record's Location is a customer or a vendor Location.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not internal and belongs to no Warehouse, so it contributes no row.

edge_cases.case: The record's Location is a transit Location.
edge_cases.outcome: It qualifies even though it may belong to no Warehouse.

edge_cases.case: The record holds a negative quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The negative figure is repeated on every day, exactly like a positive one.

worked_examples.description: The quantity record of the worked example of the document

expected_outputs.rows: one forecast row of plus thirty for every day from the eleventh of August to the eleventh of October

worked_examples.narrative: The thirty units the warehouse holds are repeated on every day of the window, and the movement rows then correct the days before and after each movement.

records.name: The forecast rows built from completed movements
records.purpose: Corrects the days before a completed movement backwards, because the current stock already contains its effect, which is why the sign is inverted for a done move.

operands.name: processed quantity in the product unit of an expanded row
operands.constraints: must be non-zero

operands.name: status of the move
operands.constraints: must be done for this variant

operands.name: day of the move
operands.source: the move's date truncated to the day
operands.constraints: the range ends the day before it

operands.name: start of the window
operands.constraints: the range starts there

operands.name: direction of the expanded row
operands.source: which of the two Warehouses the row carries
operands.constraints: decides the sign

preconditions.condition: The move is done and its processed quantity is non-zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant for an open move applies, or no row is emitted at all.

procedure: Take the expanded rows that are done and whose processed quantity is non-zero.
Emit one forecast row per day of the range that runs from the start of the window to the day before the move's own day.
Give each row the processed quantity in the product unit with a positive sign for an outgoing row and a negative sign for an incoming one.
Note that the sign is deliberately inverted: the current stock already contains the effect of a completed movement, so the days before it must be corrected backwards.
records.formula: for a done move: the day range runs from today − the horizon to the move's day − 1 day ; the signed quantity is + the processed quantity in the product unit for an outgoing row and − the processed quantity in the product unit for an incoming row

rounding.what: The truncation of the move's date to the day.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.method: Truncation to the start of the day.
rounding.step: Once per row, before the range is built.

result.name: the backward correction rows of a completed movement
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the daily quantity series after aggregation; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The move's day is the start of the window.
edge_cases.outcome: The range is empty and no correction row is emitted.

edge_cases.case: The move is done and outgoing.
edge_cases.outcome: The correction is positive, because the goods were still there on the days before it left.

edge_cases.case: The move is done and incoming.
edge_cases.outcome: The correction is negative, because the goods were not yet there on the days before it arrived.

worked_examples.description: The done receipt of the worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The five units are already inside the thirty the warehouse holds today, so every day before the receipt is corrected by minus five, which is why the forecast reads twenty-five up to the fourth of September.

records.name: The forecast rows built from open movements
records.purpose: Corrects every day from a planned movement onwards, because the current stock does not yet contain its effect.

operands.name: demand in the product unit of an expanded row
operands.constraints: must be non-zero

operands.name: status of the move
operands.constraints: must not be done for this variant

operands.name: day of the move
operands.source: the move's date truncated to the day
operands.constraints: the range starts at the later of it and the start of the window

operands.name: end of the window
operands.constraints: the range ends there

operands.name: direction of the expanded row
operands.source: which of the two Warehouses the row carries
operands.constraints: decides the sign

preconditions.condition: The move is not done and its demand is non-zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant for a completed move applies, or no row is emitted at all.

procedure: Take the expanded rows that are not done and whose demand is non-zero.
Emit one forecast row per day of the range that runs from the later of the move's day and the start of the window, to the end of the window.
Give each row the demand in the product unit with a negative sign for an outgoing row and a positive sign for an incoming one.
records.formula: for a move that is not done: the day range runs from the later of the move's day and today − the horizon , to today + the horizon ; the signed quantity is − the demand in the product unit for an outgoing row and + the demand in the product unit for an incoming row

rounding.what: The truncation of the move's date to the day.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.method: Truncation to the start of the day.
rounding.step: Once per row, before the range is built.

result.name: the forward correction rows of a planned movement
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the daily quantity series after aggregation; the series stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The move's day is before the start of the window.
edge_cases.outcome: The range starts at the start of the window, because the later of the two is taken.

edge_cases.case: The move's day is after the end of the window.
edge_cases.outcome: The range is empty and no correction is emitted.

edge_cases.case: The move is open and outgoing.
edge_cases.outcome: The correction is negative from its day onwards, because the goods will leave.

worked_examples.description: The planned delivery of the worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: Every day from the twentieth of September to the end of the window is corrected by minus eight, which is why the forecast falls to twenty-two from that day onwards.

records.name: Aggregating the daily quantity series
records.purpose: Sums the rows of the series into one figure per product, state, day, company and warehouse, and gives each aggregated row an identifier that cannot collide between the two sources.

operands.name: rows of the three kinds
operands.source: the planned movement rows and the two kinds of forecast row
operands.constraints: grouped before they are summed

operands.name: grouping key
operands.unit_or_currency: product, product template, state, date, company and warehouse
operands.constraints: the six members of the key

operands.name: underlying identifiers
operands.source: the moves and the quantity records the rows were built from
operands.constraints: the smallest of the group becomes the row identifier

preconditions.condition: The rows built from quantity records carry the negated record identifier.
preconditions.otherwise: A row built from a record could collide with a row built from a move.

procedure: Group every row by product, product template, state, date, company and warehouse.
Sum the quantities within each group.
Take the smallest underlying identifier of the group as the row's identifier.
Use the negated record identifier for the rows built from quantity records, so that they cannot collide with the rows built from moves.
records.formula: aggregated quantity = the sum of the quantities of the rows sharing the key of product , product template , state , date , company and warehouse ; the row identifier = the smallest underlying identifier of the group , the rows built from quantity records carrying the negated record identifier

rounding.what: Nothing; the sums are exact.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the aggregated rows of the daily quantity series
result.stored_or_displayed: Read-only and regenerated on every read; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: A day carries both a baseline row and a correction row.
edge_cases.outcome: They share the key and are summed, which is how the forecast of a day is produced.

edge_cases.case: Two warehouses hold the same product.
edge_cases.outcome: Their rows differ by the warehouse member of the key and are not summed together.

edge_cases.case: A row built from a record and a row built from a move would share an identifier.
edge_cases.outcome: They cannot, because the record's identifier is negated.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The baseline of thirty is corrected by minus five on every day up to the fourth of September, because the receipt is already inside it, and by minus eight from the twentieth of September onwards, so the aggregated forecast reads twenty-five, then thirty, then twenty-two.

records.name: The rules diagram of a product
records.purpose: Draws, for one product and a set of Warehouses, the graph of Locations and the rules that can move it between them, marking the rules the product would really take.

operands.name: chosen Warehouses
operands.constraints: the Routes are collected per Warehouse

operands.name: Routes that apply
operands.source: the Routes selected on the product, on the product's category chain, on the Warehouse, and the Warehouse's own generated Routes
operands.constraints: united per Warehouse

operands.name: rules of those Routes
operands.constraints: only those whose Warehouse is the chosen one or none

operands.name: attributes of each rule
operands.unit_or_currency: an Operation Type, an action, a supply method and a lead time
operands.constraints: shown as the label of the edge

preconditions.condition: At least one Warehouse is chosen.
preconditions.otherwise: No Route is collected and the diagram is empty.

procedure: For each chosen Warehouse, collect the Routes that apply: the Routes selected on the product, the Routes selected on the product's category chain, the Routes selected on that Warehouse, and the Warehouse's own generated Routes.
From those Routes, collect the rules whose Warehouse is the chosen one or none.
Lay them out as a graph whose nodes are Locations and whose edges are rules, each edge labelled with the rule's Operation Type, its action, its supply method and its lead time.
Mark the rules the product would actually take, by running the rule-matching selection for that product at each destination Location in turn.
records.formula: the nodes of the graph are the Locations named by the collected rules ; the edges are the rules whose Warehouse is the chosen one or none ; an edge is marked when the rule-matching selection for the product at that destination Location returns it

rounding.what: Nothing; the diagram shows rules and Locations.
rounding.precision: Not applicable; the lead times are shown in whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the graph of Locations and rules
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the routes report; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: A rule names another Warehouse.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not collected, only the rules of the chosen Warehouse or of none being shown.

edge_cases.case: The product names no Route of its own.
edge_cases.outcome: The Routes of its category chain and of the Warehouse still apply.

edge_cases.case: Two rules can reach the same destination Location.
edge_cases.outcome: Both are drawn, and only the one the rule-matching selection returns is marked.

worked_examples.description: A product delivered in two steps from one warehouse
worked_examples.narrative: The two rules of the delivery Route are drawn as two edges between three Locations, and both are marked because the product would really take them.

related_rules: business-rules.md permission check on the advanced-routing group

records.name: The date stamping of a detail line
records.purpose: Collects every event that sets the date of a detail line, so that the date always marks the instant the line last became more real rather than the instant of any edit.

operands.name: event acting on the line
operands.unit_or_currency: a creation, a write, a completion or a write on the move
operands.constraints: each event has one effect

operands.name: picked flag before and after
operands.source: the line and the written values
operands.constraints: a change from not picked to picked re-stamps

operands.name: quantity in the product unit before and after
operands.source: the line and the written values
operands.constraints: an increase on a picked line re-stamps

operands.name: status of the line
operands.constraints: draft, cancelled and done lines are not automatically re-stamped

operands.name: explicitly written date
operands.constraints: always wins

preconditions.condition: The event is one of those listed.
preconditions.otherwise: The date is left as it stands.

procedure: Stamp the current instant when the line is created, which is the field's own default.
Stamp the current instant when the line becomes picked while it was not.
Stamp the current instant when the line is already picked and its quantity in the product unit increases.
Leave the date unchanged when the line is already picked and its quantity decreases.
Stamp the current instant on every surviving line at the end of the completion.
Copy the move's new date onto its lines when the move's date is written while the move is done.
Apply no automatic re-stamping when the line's status is draft, cancelled or done.
Let an explicitly written date win, with no automatic re-stamping in that operation.
records.formula: line date = the current instant at creation , when the line becomes picked , when a picked line's quantity increases , and for every surviving line at the end of the completion ; = the move's new date when the move's date is written while the move is done ; = the explicit value when one is written ; unchanged otherwise

rounding.what: The comparison of the new quantity against the old one, both converted into the product unit.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the product unit.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for the conversions.
rounding.step: Once per write.

result.name: the date of the detail line
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the line and read by the traceability walk and by the put-away rule that looks for the most recently used Location.

edge_cases.case: A done move's date is written by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The new date is copied onto the lines, which is the one case where a done line's date changes.

edge_cases.case: A line's quantity falls while it is picked.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A date is written in the same operation as a quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The explicit value wins.

edge_cases.case: A line is created on a done Transfer.
edge_cases.outcome: It takes the current instant at creation like any other line.

worked_examples.description: The life of one line from creation to completion
worked_examples.narrative: Four of the five events move the date to the present and only the decrease leaves it, because the line did not become more real.

records.name: The orderings that change the records produced
records.purpose: Collects every ordering of the domain that decides which records are created rather than only how they are displayed, so that a rebuild reproduces the same choices.

operands.name: ordering of the gathering
operands.unit_or_currency: an order over Stock Quantity records
operands.source: the removal strategy and the final lot-first sort
operands.constraints: decides which goods leave

operands.name: ordering of a reduction of a processed quantity
operands.constraints: decides which promise is given back

operands.name: ordering of the freeing of reservations
operands.source: the current Transfer first, then the scheduled date descending, then the identifier descending
operands.constraints: decides whose goods are taken

operands.name: ordering of the reservation passes
operands.source: the availability check, the daily job and the re-reservation search
operands.constraints: decides who gets scarce goods

operands.name: ordering of the reception report
operands.unit_or_currency: an order over demands and over offered moves
operands.constraints: decides which demand is offered the arrival first

operands.name: ordering of the put-away rule walk and of the move merging
operands.unit_or_currency: orders over rules and over moves
operands.source: the specificity sort and the candidate sets
operands.constraints: decide which shelf is chosen and which record keeps the identifier

operands.name: ordering of the detail lines at completion
operands.source: the destination container descending, then the identifier ascending
operands.constraints: decides the consistency of the container snapshots

preconditions.condition: The ordering is applied exactly as stated.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation produces different records, not merely a different display.

procedure: Order the gathering under first in first out by incoming date ascending and then identifier ascending, which decides which goods leave.
Order it under last in first out by incoming date descending and then identifier descending.
Order it under closest location by full location name ascending compared as text and then identifier descending, so that a shelf numbered ten sorts before one numbered two.
Apply, as the final pass of every gathering, the stable sort that puts records with a lot before records without one, which guarantees that tracked stock is consumed before untracked pockets.
Walk the detail lines in reverse identifier order when reducing a processed quantity, so that the goods reserved last are given back first.
Order the candidates of the freeing of reservations by the current Transfer first, then by scheduled date descending, then by identifier descending.
Order the availability check of a Transfer by priority descending, having a deadline before not having one, deadline ascending, date ascending and identifier ascending.
Order the daily reservation job by reservation date, priority descending, date ascending and identifier ascending.
Order the re-reservation after a completion by priority descending, date ascending and identifier ascending, then place the moves sharing a document reference with the completing moves first.
Order the reception report's demands by reservation date, priority descending, date and identifier, and walk the offered incoming moves from the last to the first.
Sort the put-away rules by container type, then product, then own category, then any category, all compared as truth values in descending order, with ties keeping priority ascending then product.
Form the merge candidate sets from the whole move list of each Transfer, keep each group's natural order and let the first move of a group survive.

Order the detail lines at completion by destination container descending and then identifier ascending, so that packed lines are completed before loose ones and the container snapshots stay consistent.

Treat the ordering of the Transfer list, by priority descending, scheduled date ascending and identifier descending, and of the Operation Types, by favourite first, then sequence, then identifier, as display only.
records.formula: each ordering listed is applied exactly as stated ; the orderings of the Transfer list and of the Operation Types are display only and change no record

rounding.what: Nothing; the orderings compare dates, names and identifiers.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: No rounding occurs at any step.

result.name: the ordered sets consumed by the algorithms
result.stored_or_displayed: Each ordering is consumed by its own algorithm; the two display orderings only affect what a person sees.

edge_cases.case: A location name ends in a number.
edge_cases.outcome: The closest-location ordering compares it as text, so a shelf numbered ten sorts before one numbered two.

edge_cases.case: Two moves of a merge group are equally eligible.
edge_cases.outcome: The first of the group survives and keeps its identifier.

edge_cases.case: A line carries a destination container at completion.
edge_cases.outcome: It is completed before the loose lines, because the sort is by destination container descending.

edge_cases.case: The reception report offers several arrivals.
edge_cases.outcome: They are walked from the last to the first, so the most recently offered arrival is consumed first.

worked_examples.description: Two lines of one move at completion, one packed and one loose
worked_examples.narrative: The packed line sorts first because the ordering is by destination container descending, so the container snapshot is written for a container whose lines have all been completed.

worked_examples.description: Two shelves whose names end in numbers, under the closest-location strategy
worked_examples.narrative: The comparison is textual, so the shelf numbered ten is offered before the one numbered two and its goods leave first.

records.name: Resolving the Location set from the reading context
records.purpose: Turns the Locations and Warehouses a reader names into the set of Locations every product quantity figure is computed over, which is the same resolution the on-hand filter and the lot quantity use.

operands.name: Location values in the calling context
operands.source: either of the two names the context may carry them under
operands.constraints: wrapped into a list when a single value is given

operands.name: Warehouse values in the calling context
operands.source: either of the two names the context may carry them under
operands.constraints: wrapped into a list when a single value is given

operands.name: searchable name fields of the two entities
operands.constraints: searched with a case-insensitive containment test

operands.name: view Locations of the Warehouses
operands.constraints: the basis of three of the four branches

operands.name: enabled companies of the reader
operands.constraints: used when neither value is given

preconditions.condition: The reader has at least one enabled company.
preconditions.otherwise: The fallback branch yields no Warehouse and therefore no Location.

procedure: Read a Location value from the calling context under either of the two names it may carry, and wrap it into a list when it is not one.
Read a Warehouse value the same way.
Resolve a value given as text by searching the corresponding entity on each of its searchable name fields with a case-insensitive containment test and taking the union of the matches.
